tool.result: 1 --- 2 title: How to migrate from Pages to the App Router 3 nav_title: App Router 4 description: Learn how to upgrade your existing Next.js application from the Pages Router to the App Router. 5 --- 6 7 This guide will help you: 8 9 - [Update your Next.js application from version 12 to version 13](#nextjs-version) 10 - [Upgrade features that work in both the `pages` and the `app` directories](#upgrading-new-features) 11 - [Incrementally migrate your existing application from `pages` to `app`](#migrating-from-pages-to-app) 12 13 ## Upgrading 14 15 ### Node.js Version 16 17 The minimum Node.js version is now **v18.17**. See the [Node.js documentation](https://nodejs.org/docs/latest-v18.x/api/) for more information. 18 19 ### Next.js Version 20 21 To update to Next.js version 13, run the following command using your preferred package manager: 22 23 ```bash package="pnpm" 24 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 25 ``` 26 27 ```bash package="npm" 28 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 29 ``` 30 31 ```bash package="yarn" 32 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 33 ``` 34 35 ```bash package="bun" 36 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 37 ``` 38 39 ### ESLint Version 40 41 If you're using ESLint, you need to upgrade your ESLint version: 42 43 ```bash package="pnpm" 44 pnpm add -D eslint-config-next@latest 45 ``` 46 47 ```bash package="npm" 48 npm install -D eslint-config-next@latest 49 ``` 50 51 ```bash package="yarn" 52 yarn add -D eslint-config-next@latest 53 ``` 54 55 ```bash package="bun" 56 bun add -D eslint-config-next@latest 57 ``` 58 59 > **Good to know**: You may need to restart the ESLint server in VS Code for the ESLint changes to take effect. Open the Command Palette (`cmd+shift+p` on Mac; `ctrl+shift+p` on Windows) and search for `ESLint: Restart ESLint Server`. 60 61 ## Next Steps 62 63 After you've updated, see the following sections for next steps: 64 65 - [Upgrade new features](#upgrading-new-features): A guide to help you upgrade to new features such as the improved Image and Link Components. 66 - [Migrate from the `pages` to `app` directory](#migrating-from-pages-to-app): A step-by-step guide to help you incrementally migrate from the `pages` to the `app` directory. 67 68 ## Upgrading New Features 69 70 Next.js 13 introduced the new [App Router](/docs/app) with new features and conventions. The new Router is available in the `app` directory and co-exists with the `pages` directory. 71 72 Upgrading to Next.js 13 does **not** require using the App Router. You can continue using `pages` with new features that work in both directories, such as the updated [Image component](#image-component), [Link component](#link-component), [Script component](#script-component), and [Font optimization](#font-optimization). 73 74 ### `` Component 75 76 Next.js 12 introduced new improvements to the Image Component with a temporary import: `next/future/image`. These improvements included less client-side JavaScript, easier ways to extend and style images, better accessibility, and native browser lazy loading. 77 78 In version 13, this new behavior is now the default for `next/image`. 79 80 There are two codemods to help you migrate to the new Image Component: 81 82 - [**`next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-to-legacy-image): Safely and automatically renames `next/image` imports to `next/legacy/image`. Existing components will maintain the same behavior. 83 - [**`next-image-experimental` codemod**](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#next-image-experimental): Dangerously adds inline styles and removes unused props. This will change the behavior of existing components to match the new defaults. To use this codemod, you need to run the `next-image-to-legacy-image` codemod first. 84 85 ### `` Component 86 87 The [`` Component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) no longer requires manually adding an `` tag as a child. This behavior was added as an experimental option in [version 12.2](https://nextjs.org/blog/next-12-2) and is now the default. In Next.js 13, `` always renders `` and allows you to forward props to the underlying tag. 88 89 For example: 90 91 ```jsx 92 import Link from 'next/link' 93 94 // Next.js 12: `` has to be nested otherwise it's excluded 95 96 About 97 98 99 // Next.js 13: `` always renders `` under the hood 100 101 About 102 103 ``` 104 105 To upgrade your links to Next.js 13, you can use the [`new-link` codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#new-link). 106 107 ### `

1 --- 2 title: How to upgrade to version 16 3 nav_title: Version 16 4 description: Upgrade your Next.js Application from Version 15 to 16. 5 --- 6 7 {/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `Content` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */} 8 9 ## Use an AI agent (recommended) 10 11 An AI coding agent can run the mechanical parts of the upgrade, inspect the diff, fix follow-up breakages, and verify the app. The prompt below asks the agent to read version-matched docs, use the codemods where appropriate, explain important changes, and verify the result. Some runtime verification tools are only available after the app is upgraded. 12 13 Give the agent this prompt: 14 15 ```prompt 16 Upgrade this app to Next.js 16. 17 18 Before editing code, make sure AGENTS.md points at version-matched Next.js docs. If it is missing or outdated, follow [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs), then read AGENTS.md. 19 20 Then follow the [Next.js 16 upgrade guide](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16) as the source of truth for the migration. Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#using-the-codemod) when you're ready to run the mechanical upgrade. 21 22 Briefly explain the upgrade plan in user-facing language before making broad changes. Follow the documented defaults and keep moving unless the guide requires a project-specific decision, the change is destructive, credentials or environment setup are missing, or the correct migration is ambiguous. Keep the migration scoped to the upgrade, inspect the diff, run the relevant checks, and fix remaining breaking changes. 23 24 After the app is upgraded, use the runtime verification flow from the [AI Coding Agents guide](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents) to confirm it still works. Prefer the `next-dev-loop` skill when it is available (Next.js 16.3 or later with Turbopack); otherwise fall back to the best available `next dev`, browser, and build checks. Open the key interactive UI states and check the Next dev indicator plus browser and server logs. Summarize what changed, what was verified, and what could not be verified. 25 26 Before finishing, repeat the post-upgrade check in [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs) so the project is ready for future agent work. 27 ``` 28 29 ## Or upgrade manually 30 31 Upgrading manually follows a few steps, in order: 32 33 1. [Set up AI agent docs](#set-up-ai-agent-docs) if you use an assistant now or want future agent work grounded in version-matched docs. 34 2. [Run the upgrade codemod](#using-the-codemod). 35 3. If you prefer not to run the codemod, [install packages manually](#install-packages-manually). 36 4. Continue through the breaking changes below, run the relevant checks, and fix any remaining issues. 37 38 ## Set up AI agent docs 39 40 The prompt above asks the agent to do this before it edits code. You can also prepare the project yourself before starting the upgrade. See the [AI Coding Agents guide](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents) for the full setup. 41 42 ```bash filename="Terminal" 43 npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md 44 ``` 45 46 After upgrading, verify `AGENTS.md` still points at the docs for the installed Next.js version. On Next.js 16.2 and later, that should be the bundled docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`. If the pre-upgrade setup downloaded docs into `.next-docs/`, update `AGENTS.md` to point at the bundled docs, then remove `.next-docs/` once nothing references it. 47 48 The managed block should look like this: 49 50 ```md filename="AGENTS.md" 51 52 53 # This is NOT the Next.js you know 54 55 This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices. 56 57 This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean. 58 59 60 ``` 61 62 ## Using the codemod 63 64 To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 65 66 ```bash package="pnpm" 67 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 68 ``` 69 70 ```bash package="npm" 71 npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 72 ``` 73 74 ```bash package="yarn" 75 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 76 ``` 77 78 ```bash package="bun" 79 bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 80 ``` 81 82 The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 83 84 - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 85 - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 86 - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 87 - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 88 - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 89 90 The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod: 91 92 ```bash filename="Terminal" 93 npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api . 94 ``` 95 96 ## Install packages manually 97 98 If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 99 100 ```bash package="pnpm" 101 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 102 ``` 103 104 ```bash package="npm" 105 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 106 ``` 107 108 ```bash package="yarn" 109 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 110 ``` 111 112 ```bash package="bun" 113 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 114 ``` 115 116 If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 117 118 ## Node.js runtime and browser support 119 120 | Requirement | Change / Details | 121 | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 122 | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 123 | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 124 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 125 126 ## Turbopack by default 127 128 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 129 130 Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 131 132 ```json filename="package.json" 133 { 134 "scripts": { 135 "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 136 "build": "next build --turbopack", 137 "start": "next start" 138 } 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 143 144 ```json filename="package.json" 145 { 146 "scripts": { 147 "dev": "next dev", 148 "build": "next build", 149 "start": "next start" 150 } 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 155 156 You have a few different ways to address this: 157 158 - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 159 - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 160 - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 161 162 > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 163 164 ### Opting out of Turbopack 165 166 If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 167 168 ```json filename="package.json" 169 { 170 "scripts": { 171 "dev": "next dev", 172 "build": "next build --webpack", 173 "start": "next start" 174 } 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 179 180 ### Turbopack configuration location 181 182 The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 183 184 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 185 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 186 187 // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 188 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 189 experimental: { 190 turbopack: { 191 // options 192 }, 193 }, 194 } 195 196 export default nextConfig 197 ``` 198 199 You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 200 201 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 202 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 203 204 // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 205 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 206 turbopack: { 207 // options 208 }, 209 } 210 211 export default nextConfig 212 ``` 213 214 Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 215 216 - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 217 - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 218 219 ### Resolve alias fallback 220 221 In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 222 223 When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 224 225 However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 226 227 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 228 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 229 230 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 231 turbopack: { 232 resolveAlias: { 233 fs: { 234 browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 235 }, 236 }, 237 }, 238 } 239 240 export default nextConfig 241 ``` 242 243 It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 244 245 ### Sass node_modules imports 246 247 Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 248 249 In Webpack: 250 251 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 252 @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 253 ``` 254 255 In Turbopack: 256 257 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 258 @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 259 ``` 260 261 If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 262 263 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 264 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 265 266 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 267 turbopack: { 268 resolveAlias: { 269 '~*': '*', 270 }, 271 }, 272 } 273 274 export default nextConfig 275 ``` 276 277 ### Turbopack File System Caching 278 279 Turbopack stores compiler artifacts on disk between runs, for significantly faster compile times across restarts. Filesystem caching is enabled by default for both `next dev` and `next build`, through `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` and `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`. See [Turbopack FileSystem Caching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopackFileSystemCache) to configure or disable either one. 280 281 ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 282 283 Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 284 285 Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 286 287 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 288 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 289 - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 290 - `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon). 291 - `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) 292 293 Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs. 294 295 ### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs 296 297 To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers: 298 299 - [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) 300 - [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) 301 - [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) 302 303 > **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5 304 305 This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example: 306 307 ```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 308 export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 309 const { slug } = await props.params 310 const query = await props.searchParams 311 return

Blog Post: {slug}

312 } 313 ``` 314 315 This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page. 316 317 ## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change) 318 319 > The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises. 320 321 In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function. 322 323 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 324 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params access 325 export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 326 const { slug } = params 327 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 328 } 329 330 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access 331 export default function Image({ params, id }) { 332 const slug = params.slug 333 const imageId = id // string 334 // ... 335 } 336 ``` 337 338 Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`. 339 340 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 341 export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 342 const { slug } = params 343 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 344 } 345 346 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access 347 export default async function Image({ params, id }) { 348 const { slug } = await params // params now async 349 const imageId = await id // id is now Promise when using generateImageMetadata 350 // ... 351 } 352 ``` 353 354 ## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change) 355 356 Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function. 357 358 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 359 export async function generateSitemaps() { 360 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 361 } 362 363 // Next.js 15 - synchronous id access 364 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 365 const start = id * 50000 // id is a number 366 // ... 367 } 368 ``` 369 370 Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise. 371 372 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 373 export async function generateSitemaps() { 374 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 375 } 376 377 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access 378 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 379 const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise 380 const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000 381 // ... 382 } 383 ``` 384 385 ## React 19.2 386 387 The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include: 388 389 - **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation 390 - **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions 391 - **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects 392 393 Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2). 394 395 ## React Compiler Support 396 397 Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 398 399 The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 400 401 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 402 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 403 404 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 405 reactCompiler: true, 406 } 407 408 export default nextConfig 409 ``` 410 411 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 412 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 413 const nextConfig = { 414 reactCompiler: true, 415 } 416 417 module.exports = nextConfig 418 ``` 419 420 Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 421 422 ```bash package="pnpm" 423 pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 424 ``` 425 426 ```bash package="npm" 427 npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 428 ``` 429 430 ```bash package="yarn" 431 yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 432 ``` 433 434 ```bash package="bun" 435 bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 436 ``` 437 438 > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 439 440 ## Caching APIs 441 442 ### revalidateTag 443 444 [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 445 446 ```ts 447 // Before 448 revalidateTag('posts') 449 450 // After 451 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 452 ``` 453 454 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 455 456 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 457 'use server' 458 459 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 460 461 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 462 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 463 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 464 } 465 ``` 466 467 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 468 'use server' 469 470 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 471 472 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 473 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 474 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 479 480 ### updateTag 481 482 [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 483 484 It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 485 486 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 487 'use server' 488 489 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 490 491 export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 492 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 493 494 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 495 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 496 } 497 ``` 498 499 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 500 'use server' 501 502 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 503 504 export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 505 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 506 507 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 508 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly. 513 514 Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag). 515 516 ### refresh 517 518 [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action. 519 520 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 521 'use server' 522 523 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 524 525 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) { 526 // Update the notification in the database 527 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 528 529 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 530 refresh() 531 } 532 ``` 533 534 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 535 'use server' 536 537 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 538 539 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) { 540 // Update the notification in the database 541 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 542 543 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 544 refresh() 545 } 546 ``` 547 548 Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action. 549 550 ### cacheLife and cacheTag 551 552 [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 553 554 Wherever you had aliased imports like: 555 556 ```ts 557 import { 558 unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 559 unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 560 } from 'next/cache' 561 ``` 562 563 You can update your imports to: 564 565 ```ts 566 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 567 ``` 568 569 ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 570 571 **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 572 573 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 574 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 575 576 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 577 578 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 579 580 If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 581 582 ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 583 584 **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 585 586 Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 587 588 ```js filename="next.config.js" 589 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 590 const nextConfig = { 591 cacheComponents: true, 592 } 593 594 module.exports = nextConfig 595 ``` 596 597 PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 598 599 ```js filename="next.config.js" 600 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 601 const nextConfig = { 602 // If you are using PPR today 603 // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 604 experimental: { 605 ppr: true, 606 }, 607 } 608 609 module.exports = nextConfig 610 ``` 611 612 ## `middleware` to `proxy` 613 614 The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 615 616 The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions. 617 618 ```bash filename="Terminal" 619 # Rename your middleware file 620 mv middleware.ts proxy.ts 621 # or 622 mv middleware.js proxy.js 623 ``` 624 625 The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`. 626 627 ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher 628 export function proxy(request: Request) {} 629 ``` 630 631 ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher 632 export function proxy(request) {} 633 ``` 634 635 We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export. 636 637 Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize` 638 639 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 640 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 641 642 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 643 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 644 } 645 646 export default nextConfig 647 ``` 648 649 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 650 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 651 const nextConfig = { 652 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 653 } 654 655 module.exports = nextConfig 656 ``` 657 658 The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too. 659 660 ## `next/image` changes 661 662 ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 663 664 Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 665 666 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 667 import Image from 'next/image' 668 669 export default function Page() { 670 return 671 } 672 ``` 673 674 If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 675 676 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 677 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 678 679 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 680 images: { 681 localPatterns: [ 682 { 683 pathname: '/assets/**', 684 search: '?v=1', 685 }, 686 ], 687 }, 688 } 689 690 export default nextConfig 691 ``` 692 693 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 694 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 695 const nextConfig = { 696 images: { 697 localPatterns: [ 698 { 699 pathname: '/assets/**', 700 search: '?v=1', 701 }, 702 ], 703 }, 704 } 705 706 module.exports = nextConfig 707 ``` 708 709 ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 710 711 The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 712 713 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 714 715 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 716 717 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 718 719 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 720 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 721 722 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 723 images: { 724 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 725 }, 726 } 727 728 export default nextConfig 729 ``` 730 731 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 732 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 733 const nextConfig = { 734 images: { 735 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 736 }, 737 } 738 739 module.exports = nextConfig 740 ``` 741 742 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 743 744 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 745 746 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 747 748 If you need to support 16px images: 749 750 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 751 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 752 753 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 754 images: { 755 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 756 }, 757 } 758 759 export default nextConfig 760 ``` 761 762 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 763 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 764 const nextConfig = { 765 images: { 766 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 767 }, 768 } 769 770 module.exports = nextConfig 771 ``` 772 773 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 774 775 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 776 777 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 778 779 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 780 781 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 782 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 783 784 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 785 images: { 786 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 787 }, 788 } 789 790 export default nextConfig 791 ``` 792 793 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 794 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 795 const nextConfig = { 796 images: { 797 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 798 }, 799 } 800 801 module.exports = nextConfig 802 ``` 803 804 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 805 806 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 807 808 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 809 810 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 811 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 812 813 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 814 images: { 815 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 816 }, 817 } 818 819 export default nextConfig 820 ``` 821 822 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 823 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 824 const nextConfig = { 825 images: { 826 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 827 }, 828 } 829 830 module.exports = nextConfig 831 ``` 832 833 This might be necessary when hosting Next.js in a VPC with split-horizon DNS and you receive status 400 Bad Request. Only enable once you understand the SSRF risk. 834 835 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 836 837 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 838 839 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 840 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 841 842 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 843 images: { 844 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 845 // or 846 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 847 }, 848 } 849 850 export default nextConfig 851 ``` 852 853 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 854 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 855 const nextConfig = { 856 images: { 857 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 858 // or 859 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 860 }, 861 } 862 863 module.exports = nextConfig 864 ``` 865 866 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 867 868 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 869 870 ```tsx 871 // Before 872 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 873 874 // After 875 import Image from 'next/image' 876 ``` 877 878 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 879 880 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 881 882 ```js filename="next.config.js" 883 // image.domains is deprecated 884 module.exports = { 885 images: { 886 domains: ['example.com'], 887 }, 888 } 889 ``` 890 891 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 892 893 ```js filename="next.config.js" 894 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 895 module.exports = { 896 images: { 897 remotePatterns: [ 898 { 899 protocol: 'https', 900 hostname: 'example.com', 901 }, 902 ], 903 }, 904 } 905 ``` 906 907 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 908 909 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 910 911 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 912 913 The [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 914 915 ```bash package="pnpm" 916 pnpm next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 917 ``` 918 919 ```bash package="npm" 920 npx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 921 ``` 922 923 ```bash package="yarn" 924 yarn next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 925 ``` 926 927 ```bash package="bun" 928 bunx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 929 ``` 930 931 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 932 933 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 934 935 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 936 937 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 938 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 939 940 export default function Default() { 941 notFound() 942 } 943 ``` 944 945 Or return `null`: 946 947 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 948 export default function Default() { 949 return null 950 } 951 ``` 952 953 ## ESLint Flat Config 954 955 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 956 957 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 958 959 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 960 961 ## Scroll Behavior Override 962 963 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 964 965 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 966 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 967 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 968 969 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 970 971 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 972 973 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 974 975 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 976 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 977 return ( 978 979 {children} 980 981 ) 982 } 983 ``` 984 985 ## Performance Improvements 986 987 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 988 989 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 990 991 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 992 993 ### `next dev` config load 994 995 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 996 997 - When running the `next dev` command 998 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 999 1000 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1001 1002 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1003 1004 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1005 1006 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1007 1008 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1009 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1010 1011 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1012 1013 if (isDev) { 1014 startServer() 1015 } 1016 1017 const nextConfig = { 1018 /* Your config options */ 1019 } 1020 1021 module.exports = nextConfig 1022 ``` 1023 1024 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1025 1026 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1027 1028 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1029 1030 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1031 1032 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1033 const nextConfig = { 1034 experimental: { 1035 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1036 }, 1037 } 1038 1039 module.exports = nextConfig 1040 ``` 1041 1042 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. 1156 } 1157 ``` 1158 1159 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1160 1161 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1162 1163 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1164 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1165 ``` 1166 1167 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1168 'use client' 1169 1170 export default function ClientComponent() { 1171 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1172 return

API URL: {apiUrl}

1173 } 1174 ``` 1175 1176 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1179 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1180 1181 export default async function Page() { 1182 await connection() 1183 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1184 return

{config}

1185 } 1186 ``` 1187 1188 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1189 1190 ### `devIndicators` Options 1191 1192 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1193 1194 - `appIsrStatus` 1195 - `buildActivity` 1196 - `buildActivityPosition` 1197 1198 The indicator itself remains available. 1199 1200 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1201 1202 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags have been removed. 1203 1204 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1205 // Before: experimental.useCache 1206 module.exports = { 1207 experimental: { 1208 useCache: true, 1209 }, 1210 } 1211 ``` 1212 1213 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1214 // Before: experimental.dynamicIO 1215 module.exports = { 1216 experimental: { 1217 dynamicIO: true, 1218 }, 1219 } 1220 ``` 1221 1222 If you were actively using these flags, migrate to top-level [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents): 1223 1224 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 1225 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 1226 1227 // After 1228 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 1229 cacheComponents: true, 1230 } 1231 1232 export default nextConfig 1233 ``` 1234 1235 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 1236 // After 1237 module.exports = { 1238 cacheComponents: true, 1239 } 1240 ``` 1241 1242 If you were not actively adopting Cache Components, remove the flags instead. Enabling `cacheComponents` is not a rename-only change: it can surface build errors for uncached data outside of `` and requires adopting the Cache Components model. 1243 1244 For the full migration path, see [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components). 1245 1246 ### `unstable_rootParams` 1247 1248 The `unstable_rootParams` function has been removed. Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#using-the-codemod) when you're ready to run the mechanical upgrade. 21 22 Briefly explain the upgrade plan in user-facing language before making broad changes. Follow the documented defaults and keep moving unless the guide requires a project-specific decision, the change is destructive, credentials or environment setup are missing, or the correct migration is ambiguous. Keep the migration scoped to the upgrade, inspect the diff, run the relevant checks, and fix remaining breaking changes. 23 24 After the app is upgraded, use the runtime verification flow from the [AI Coding Agents guide](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents) to confirm it still works.
