Open the key interactive UI states and check the Next dev indicator plus browser and server logs. Summarize what changed, what was verified, and what could not be verified. 25 26 Before finishing, repeat the post-upgrade check in [Set up AI agent docs](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-16#set-up-ai-agent-docs) so the project is ready for future agent work. 27 ``` 28 29 ## Or upgrade manually 30 31 Upgrading manually follows a few steps, in order: 32 33 1. [Set up AI agent docs](#set-up-ai-agent-docs) if you use an assistant now or want future agent work grounded in version-matched docs. 34 2. [Run the upgrade codemod](#using-the-codemod). 35 3. If you prefer not to run the codemod, [install packages manually](#install-packages-manually). 36 4. Continue through the breaking changes below, run the relevant checks, and fix any remaining issues. 37 38 ## Set up AI agent docs 39 40 The prompt above asks the agent to do this before it edits code. You can also prepare the project yourself before starting the upgrade. See the [AI Coding Agents guide](/docs/app/guides/ai-agents) for the full setup. 41 42 ```bash filename="Terminal" 43 npx @next/codemod@canary agents-md 44 ``` 45 46 After upgrading, verify `AGENTS.md` still points at the docs for the installed Next.js version. On Next.js 16.2 and later, that should be the bundled docs in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`. If the pre-upgrade setup downloaded docs into `.next-docs/`, update `AGENTS.md` to point at the bundled docs, then remove `.next-docs/` once nothing references it. 47 48 The managed block should look like this: 49 50 ```md filename="AGENTS.md" 51 52 53 # This is NOT the Next.js you know 54 55 This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` (resolved from this file's directory; in monorepos the `next` package may not be visible from the repo root) before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices. 56 57 This block is written and re-added by `next dev` — verify at `node_modules/next/dist/server/lib/generate-agent-files.js`. Removing it from a diff only re-creates the uncommitted change; committing it with your work keeps the tree clean. 58 59 60 ``` 61 62 ## Using the codemod 63 64 To update to Next.js version 16, you can use the `upgrade` [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160): 65 66 ```bash package="pnpm" 67 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 68 ``` 69 70 ```bash package="npm" 71 npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 72 ``` 73 74 ```bash package="yarn" 75 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 76 ``` 77 78 ```bash package="bun" 79 bunx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest 80 ``` 81 82 The [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to: 83 84 - Update `next.config.js` to use the new `turbopack` configuration 85 - Migrate from `next lint` to the ESLint CLI 86 - Migrate from deprecated `middleware` convention to `proxy` 87 - Remove `unstable_` prefix from stabilized APIs 88 - Remove `experimental_ppr` Route Segment Config from pages and layouts 89 90 The `upgrade` codemod does not run every migration codemod. If your app still uses synchronous `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `draftMode()` access from the Next.js 15 compatibility period, also run the async Request APIs codemod: 91 92 ```bash filename="Terminal" 93 npx @next/codemod@canary next-async-request-api . 94 ``` 95 96 ## Install packages manually 97 98 If you prefer to do it manually, install the latest Next.js and React versions: 99 100 ```bash package="pnpm" 101 pnpm add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 102 ``` 103 104 ```bash package="npm" 105 npm install next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 106 ``` 107 108 ```bash package="yarn" 109 yarn add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 110 ``` 111 112 ```bash package="bun" 113 bun add next@latest react@latest react-dom@latest 114 ``` 115 116 If you are using TypeScript, ensure you also upgrade `@types/react` and `@types/react-dom` to their latest versions. 117 118 ## Node.js runtime and browser support 119 120 | Requirement | Change / Details | 121 | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | 122 | Node.js 20.9+ | Minimum version now `20.9.0` (LTS); Node.js 18 no longer supported | 123 | TypeScript 5+ | Minimum version now `5.1.0` | 124 | Browsers | Chrome 111+, Edge 111+, Firefox 111+, Safari 16.4+ | 125 126 ## Turbopack by default 127 128 Starting with **Next.js 16**, Turbopack is stable and used by default with `next dev` and `next build` 129 130 Previously you had to enable Turbopack using `--turbopack`, or `--turbo`. 131 132 ```json filename="package.json" 133 { 134 "scripts": { 135 "dev": "next dev --turbopack", 136 "build": "next build --turbopack", 137 "start": "next start" 138 } 139 } 140 ``` 141 142 This is no longer necessary. You can update your `package.json` scripts: 143 144 ```json filename="package.json" 145 { 146 "scripts": { 147 "dev": "next dev", 148 "build": "next build", 149 "start": "next start" 150 } 151 } 152 ``` 153 154 If your project has a [custom `webpack`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/webpack) configuration and you run `next build` (which now uses Turbopack by default), the build will **fail** to prevent misconfiguration issues. 155 156 You have a few different ways to address this: 157 158 - **Use Turbopack anyway:** Run with `next build --turbopack` to build using Turbopack and ignore your `webpack` config. 159 - **Switch to Turbopack fully:** Migrate your `webpack` config to Turbopack-compatible options. 160 - **Keep using Webpack:** Use the `--webpack` flag to opt out of Turbopack and build with Webpack. 161 162 > **Good to know**: If you see failing builds because a `webpack` configuration was found, but you don't define one yourself, it is likely that a plugin is adding a `webpack` option 163 164 ### Opting out of Turbopack 165 166 If you need to continue using Webpack, you can opt out with the `--webpack` flag. For example, to use Turbopack in development but Webpack for production builds: 167 168 ```json filename="package.json" 169 { 170 "scripts": { 171 "dev": "next dev", 172 "build": "next build --webpack", 173 "start": "next start" 174 } 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 We recommend using Turbopack for development and production. Submit a comment to this [thread](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77721), if you are unable to switch to Turbopack. 179 180 ### Turbopack configuration location 181 182 The `experimental.turbopack` configuration is out of experimental. 183 184 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 185 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 186 187 // Next.js 15 - experimental.turbopack 188 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 189 experimental: { 190 turbopack: { 191 // options 192 }, 193 }, 194 } 195 196 export default nextConfig 197 ``` 198 199 You can use it as a top-level `turbopack` option: 200 201 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 202 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 203 204 // Next.js 16 - turbopack at the top level of nextConfig 205 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 206 turbopack: { 207 // options 208 }, 209 } 210 211 export default nextConfig 212 ``` 213 214 Make sure to review the `Turbopack` configuration [options](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack). **Next.js 16** introduces various improvements and new options, for example: 215 216 - [Advanced Webpack loader conditions](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#advanced-webpack-loader-conditions) 217 - [debugIds](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopack#debug-ids) 218 219 ### Resolve alias fallback 220 221 In some projects, client-side code may import files containing Node.js native modules. This will cause `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` type of errors. 222 223 When this happens, you should refactor your code so that your client-side bundles do not reference these Node.js native modules. 224 225 However, in some cases, this might not be possible. In Webpack the `resolve.fallback` option was typically used to **silence** the error. Turbopack offers a similar option, using `turbopack.resolveAlias`. In this case, tell Turbopack to load an empty module when `fs` is requested for the browser. 226 227 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 228 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 229 230 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 231 turbopack: { 232 resolveAlias: { 233 fs: { 234 browser: './empty.ts', // We recommend to fix code imports before using this method 235 }, 236 }, 237 }, 238 } 239 240 export default nextConfig 241 ``` 242 243 It is preferable to refactor your modules so that client code doesn't ever import from modules using Node.js native modules. 244 245 ### Sass node_modules imports 246 247 Turbopack fully supports importing Sass files from `node_modules`. Note that while Webpack allowed the legacy tilde (`~`) prefix, Turbopack does not support this syntax. 248 249 In Webpack: 250 251 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 252 @import '~bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 253 ``` 254 255 In Turbopack: 256 257 ```scss filename="styles/globals.scss" 258 @import 'bootstrap/dist/css/bootstrap.min.css'; 259 ``` 260 261 If changing the imports is not possible, you can use `turbopack.resolveAlias`. For example: 262 263 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" 264 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 265 266 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 267 turbopack: { 268 resolveAlias: { 269 '~*': '*', 270 }, 271 }, 272 } 273 274 export default nextConfig 275 ``` 276 277 ### Turbopack File System Caching 278 279 Turbopack stores compiler artifacts on disk between runs, for significantly faster compile times across restarts. Filesystem caching is enabled by default for both `next dev` and `next build`, through `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForDev` and `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild`. See [Turbopack FileSystem Caching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/turbopackFileSystemCache) to configure or disable either one. 280 281 ## Async Request APIs (Breaking change) 282 283 Version 15 introduced [Async Request APIs](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/upgrading/version-15#async-request-apis-breaking-change) as a breaking change, with **temporary** synchronous compatibility. 284 285 Starting with **Next.js 16**, synchronous access is fully removed. These APIs can only be accessed asynchronously. 286 287 - [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) 288 - [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) 289 - [`draftMode`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/draft-mode) 290 - `params` in [`layout.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout), [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), [`route.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route), [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default), [`opengraph-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#opengraph-image), [`twitter-image`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/opengraph-image#twitter-image), [`icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#icon), and [`apple-icon`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/app-icons#apple-icon). 291 - `searchParams` in [`page.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) 292 293 Use the [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#migrate-to-async-dynamic-apis) to migrate to async Request-time APIs. 294 295 ### Migrating types for async Request-time APIs 296 297 To help migrate to async `params` and `searchParams`, you can run [`npx next typegen`](/docs/app/api-reference/cli/next#next-typegen-options) to automatically generate these globally available types helpers: 298 299 - [`PageProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) 300 - [`LayoutProps`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) 301 - [`RouteContext`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#route-context-helper) 302 303 > **Good to know**: `typegen` was introduced in Next.js 15.5 304 305 This simplifies type-safe migration to the new async API pattern, and enables you to update your components with full type safety, for example: 306 307 ```tsx filename="/app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 308 export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 309 const { slug } = await props.params 310 const query = await props.searchParams 311 return

Blog Post: {slug}

312 } 313 ``` 314 315 This approach gives you fully type-safe access to `props.params`, including the `slug`, and to `searchParams`, directly within your page. 316 317 ## Async parameters for icon, and open-graph Image (Breaking change) 318 319 > The props passed to the image generating functions in `opengraph-image`, `twitter-image`, `icon`, and `apple-icon`, are now Promises. 320 321 In previous versions, both the `Image` (image generation function), and the `generateImageMetadata` received a `params` object. The `id` returned by `generateImageMetadata` was passed as a string to the image generation function. 322 323 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 324 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params access 325 export function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 326 const { slug } = params 327 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 328 } 329 330 // Next.js 15 - synchronous params and id access 331 export default function Image({ params, id }) { 332 const slug = params.slug 333 const imageId = id // string 334 // ... 335 } 336 ``` 337 338 Starting with **Next.js 16**, to align with the [Async Request APIs](#async-request-apis-breaking-change) change, the image generating function now receives `params` and `id` as promises. The `generateImageMetadata` function continues to receive synchronous `params`. 339 340 ```js filename="app/shop/[slug]/opengraph-image.js" 341 export async function generateImageMetadata({ params }) { 342 const { slug } = params 343 return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }] 344 } 345 346 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous params and id access 347 export default async function Image({ params, id }) { 348 const { slug } = await params // params now async 349 const imageId = await id // id is now Promise when using generateImageMetadata 350 // ... 351 } 352 ``` 353 354 ## Async `id` parameter for `sitemap` (Breaking change) 355 356 Previously, the `id` values returned from [`generateSitemaps`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-sitemaps) were passed directly to the `sitemap` generating function. 357 358 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 359 export async function generateSitemaps() { 360 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 361 } 362 363 // Next.js 15 - synchronous id access 364 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 365 const start = id * 50000 // id is a number 366 // ... 367 } 368 ``` 369 370 Starting with **Next.js 16**, the `sitemap` generating function now receives `id` as a promise. 371 372 ```js filename="app/product/sitemap.js" 373 export async function generateSitemaps() { 374 return [{ id: 0 }, { id: 1 }, { id: 2 }, { id: 3 }] 375 } 376 377 // Next.js 16 - asynchronous id access 378 export default async function sitemap({ id }) { 379 const resolvedId = await id // id is now Promise 380 const start = Number(resolvedId) * 50000 381 // ... 382 } 383 ``` 384 385 ## React 19.2 386 387 The App Router in **Next.js 16** uses the latest React [Canary release](https://react.dev/blog/2023/05/03/react-canaries), which includes the newly released React 19.2 features and other features being incrementally stabilized. Highlights include: 388 389 - **[View Transitions](https://react.dev/reference/react/ViewTransition)**: Animate elements that update inside a Transition or navigation 390 - **[`useEffectEvent`](https://react.dev/reference/react/useEffectEvent)**: Extract non-reactive logic from Effects into reusable Effect Event functions 391 - **[Activity](https://react.dev/reference/react/Activity)**: Render "background activity" by hiding UI with `display: none` while maintaining state and cleaning up Effects 392 393 Learn more in the [React 19.2 announcement](https://react.dev/blog/2025/10/01/react-19-2). 394 395 ## React Compiler Support 396 397 Built-in support for the React Compiler is now stable in **Next.js 16** following the React Compiler's 1.0 release. The React Compiler automatically memoizes components, reducing unnecessary re-renders with zero manual code changes. 398 399 The `reactCompiler` configuration option has been promoted from `experimental` to stable. It is not enabled by default as we continue gathering build performance data across different application types. 400 401 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 402 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 403 404 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 405 reactCompiler: true, 406 } 407 408 export default nextConfig 409 ``` 410 411 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 412 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 413 const nextConfig = { 414 reactCompiler: true, 415 } 416 417 module.exports = nextConfig 418 ``` 419 420 Install the latest version of the React Compiler plugin: 421 422 ```bash package="pnpm" 423 pnpm add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 424 ``` 425 426 ```bash package="npm" 427 npm install -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 428 ``` 429 430 ```bash package="yarn" 431 yarn add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 432 ``` 433 434 ```bash package="bun" 435 bun add -D babel-plugin-react-compiler 436 ``` 437 438 > **Good to know:** Expect compile times in development and during builds to be higher when enabling this option as the React Compiler relies on Babel. 439 440 ## Caching APIs 441 442 ### revalidateTag 443 444 [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) now requires a second argument specifying a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#reference) profile. The single-argument form is deprecated and will produce a TypeScript error. 445 446 ```ts 447 // Before 448 revalidateTag('posts') 449 450 // After 451 revalidateTag('posts', 'max') 452 ``` 453 454 If you need immediate expiration rather than stale-while-revalidate, use [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) in Server Actions instead. 455 456 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 457 'use server' 458 459 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 460 461 export async function updateArticle(articleId: string) { 462 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 463 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 464 } 465 ``` 466 467 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 468 'use server' 469 470 import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache' 471 472 export async function updateArticle(articleId) { 473 // Mark article data as stale - article readers see stale data while it revalidates 474 revalidateTag(`article-${articleId}`, 'max') 475 } 476 ``` 477 478 Use `revalidateTag` for content where a slight delay in updates is acceptable, such as blog posts, product catalogs, or documentation. Users receive stale content while fresh data loads in the background. 479 480 ### updateTag 481 482 [`updateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag) is a new [Server Actions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data#what-are-server-functions)-only API that provides **read-your-writes** semantics, where a user makes a change and the UI immediately shows the change, rather than stale data. 483 484 It does this by expiring and immediately refreshing data within the same request. 485 486 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 487 'use server' 488 489 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 490 491 export async function updateUserProfile(userId: string, profile: Profile) { 492 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 493 494 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 495 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 496 } 497 ``` 498 499 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 500 'use server' 501 502 import { updateTag } from 'next/cache' 503 504 export async function updateUserProfile(userId, profile) { 505 await db.users.update(userId, profile) 506 507 // Expire cache and refresh immediately - user sees their changes right away 508 updateTag(`user-${userId}`) 509 } 510 ``` 511 512 This ensures interactive features reflect changes immediately. Perfect for forms, user settings, and any workflow where users expect to see their updates instantly. 513 514 Learn more about when to use `updateTag` or `revalidateTag` [here](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/updateTag#when-to-use-updatetag). 515 516 ### refresh 517 518 [`refresh`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/refresh) allows you to refresh the client router from within a Server Action. 519 520 ```ts filename="app/actions.ts" switcher 521 'use server' 522 523 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 524 525 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId: string) { 526 // Update the notification in the database 527 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 528 529 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 530 refresh() 531 } 532 ``` 533 534 ```js filename="app/actions.js" switcher 535 'use server' 536 537 import { refresh } from 'next/cache' 538 539 export async function markNotificationAsRead(notificationId) { 540 // Update the notification in the database 541 await db.notifications.markAsRead(notificationId) 542 543 // Refresh the notification count displayed in the header 544 refresh() 545 } 546 ``` 547 548 Use it when you need to refresh the client router after performing an action. 549 550 ### cacheLife and cacheTag 551 552 [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife) and [`cacheTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheTag) are now stable. The `unstable_` prefix is no longer needed. 553 554 Wherever you had aliased imports like: 555 556 ```ts 557 import { 558 unstable_cacheLife as cacheLife, 559 unstable_cacheTag as cacheTag, 560 } from 'next/cache' 561 ``` 562 563 You can update your imports to: 564 565 ```ts 566 import { cacheLife, cacheTag } from 'next/cache' 567 ``` 568 569 ## Enhanced Routing and Navigation 570 571 **Next.js 16** includes a complete overhaul of the routing and navigation system, making page transitions leaner and faster. This optimizes how Next.js prefetches and caches navigation data: 572 573 - **Layout deduplication**: When prefetching multiple URLs with a shared layout, the layout is downloaded once. 574 - **Incremental prefetching**: Next.js only prefetches parts not already in cache, rather than entire pages. 575 576 These changes require **no code modifications** and are designed to improve performance across all apps. 577 578 However, you may see more individual prefetch requests with much lower total transfer sizes. We believe this is the right trade-off for nearly all applications. 579 580 If the increased request count causes issues, please let us know by creating an [issue](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues) or [discussion](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions) item. 581 582 ## Partial Prerendering (PPR) 583 584 **Next.js 16** removes the experimental **Partial Prerendering (PPR)** flag and configuration options, including the route level segment `experimental_ppr`. 585 586 Starting with **Next.js 16**, you can opt into PPR using the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) configuration. 587 588 ```js filename="next.config.js" 589 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 590 const nextConfig = { 591 cacheComponents: true, 592 } 593 594 module.exports = nextConfig 595 ``` 596 597 PPR in **Next.js 16** works differently than in **Next.js 15** canaries. If you are using PPR today, stay in the current Next.js 15 canary you are using. See [Migrating to Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) for migration patterns. 598 599 ```js filename="next.config.js" 600 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 601 const nextConfig = { 602 // If you are using PPR today 603 // stay in the current Next.js 15 canary 604 experimental: { 605 ppr: true, 606 }, 607 } 608 609 module.exports = nextConfig 610 ``` 611 612 ## `middleware` to `proxy` 613 614 The `middleware` filename is deprecated, and has been renamed to `proxy` to clarify network boundary and routing focus. 615 616 The `edge` runtime is **NOT** supported in `proxy`. The `proxy` runtime is `nodejs`, and it cannot be configured. If you want to continue using the `edge` runtime, keep using `middleware`. We will follow up on a minor release with further `edge` runtime instructions. 617 618 ```bash filename="Terminal" 619 # Rename your middleware file 620 mv middleware.ts proxy.ts 621 # or 622 mv middleware.js proxy.js 623 ``` 624 625 The named export `middleware` is also deprecated. Rename your function to `proxy`. 626 627 ```ts filename="proxy.ts" switcher 628 export function proxy(request: Request) {} 629 ``` 630 631 ```js filename="proxy.js" switcher 632 export function proxy(request) {} 633 ``` 634 635 We recommend changing the function name to `proxy`, even if you are using a default export. 636 637 Configuration flags that contained the `middleware` name are also renamed. For example, `skipMiddlewareUrlNormalize` is now `skipProxyUrlNormalize` 638 639 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 640 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 641 642 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 643 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 644 } 645 646 export default nextConfig 647 ``` 648 649 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 650 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 651 const nextConfig = { 652 skipProxyUrlNormalize: true, 653 } 654 655 module.exports = nextConfig 656 ``` 657 658 The version 16 [codemod](/docs/app/guides/upgrading/codemods#160) is able to update these flags too. 659 660 ## `next/image` changes 661 662 ### Local Images with Query Strings (Breaking change) 663 664 Local image sources with query strings now require `images.localPatterns.search` configuration to prevent enumeration attacks. 665 666 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 667 import Image from 'next/image' 668 669 export default function Page() { 670 return 671 } 672 ``` 673 674 If you need to use query strings with local images, add the pattern to your configuration: 675 676 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 677 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 678 679 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 680 images: { 681 localPatterns: [ 682 { 683 pathname: '/assets/**', 684 search: '?v=1', 685 }, 686 ], 687 }, 688 } 689 690 export default nextConfig 691 ``` 692 693 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 694 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 695 const nextConfig = { 696 images: { 697 localPatterns: [ 698 { 699 pathname: '/assets/**', 700 search: '?v=1', 701 }, 702 ], 703 }, 704 } 705 706 module.exports = nextConfig 707 ``` 708 709 ### `minimumCacheTTL` Default (Breaking change) 710 711 The default value for `images.minimumCacheTTL` has changed from `60 seconds` to `4 hours` (14400 seconds). This reduces revalidation cost for images without cache-control headers. 712 713 For some Next.js users, image revalidation was happening frequently, often because the upstream source images missed a `cache-control` header. This caused revalidation to happen every `60` seconds, which increased CPU usage and cost. 714 715 Since most images do not change often, this short interval is not ideal. Setting the default to 4 hours offers a more durable cache by default, while still allowing images to update a few times per day if needed. 716 717 If you need the previous behavior, change `minimumCacheTTL` to a lower value, for example back to `60` seconds: 718 719 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 720 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 721 722 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 723 images: { 724 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 725 }, 726 } 727 728 export default nextConfig 729 ``` 730 731 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 732 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 733 const nextConfig = { 734 images: { 735 minimumCacheTTL: 60, 736 }, 737 } 738 739 module.exports = nextConfig 740 ``` 741 742 ### `imageSizes` Default (Breaking change) 743 744 The value `16` has been removed from the default `images.imageSizes` array. 745 746 We have looked at request analytics and found out that very few projects ever serve 16 pixels width images. Removing this setting reduces the size of the `srcset` attribute shipped to the browser by `next/image`. 747 748 If you need to support 16px images: 749 750 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 751 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 752 753 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 754 images: { 755 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 756 }, 757 } 758 759 export default nextConfig 760 ``` 761 762 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 763 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 764 const nextConfig = { 765 images: { 766 imageSizes: [16, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 256, 384], 767 }, 768 } 769 770 module.exports = nextConfig 771 ``` 772 773 Rather than lack of developer usage, we believe 16 pixels width images have become less common, because `devicePixelRatio: 2` actually fetches a 32px image to prevent blurriness in retina displays. 774 775 ### `qualities` Default (Breaking change) 776 777 The default value for `images.qualities` has changed from allowing all qualities to only `[75]`. 778 779 If you need to support multiple quality levels: 780 781 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 782 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 783 784 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 785 images: { 786 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 787 }, 788 } 789 790 export default nextConfig 791 ``` 792 793 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 794 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 795 const nextConfig = { 796 images: { 797 qualities: [50, 75, 100], 798 }, 799 } 800 801 module.exports = nextConfig 802 ``` 803 804 If you specify a `quality` prop not included in the `image.qualities` array, the quality will be coerced to the closest value in `images.qualities`. For example, given the configuration above, a `quality` prop of 80, is coerced to 75. 805 806 ### Local IP Restriction (Breaking change) 807 808 A new security restriction blocks local IP optimization by default. Set `images.dangerouslyAllowLocalIP` to `true` only for private networks. 809 810 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 811 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 812 813 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 814 images: { 815 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 816 }, 817 } 818 819 export default nextConfig 820 ``` 821 822 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 823 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 824 const nextConfig = { 825 images: { 826 dangerouslyAllowLocalIP: true, // Only for private networks 827 }, 828 } 829 830 module.exports = nextConfig 831 ``` 832 833 This might be necessary when hosting Next.js in a VPC with split-horizon DNS and you receive status 400 Bad Request. Only enable once you understand the SSRF risk. 834 835 ### Maximum Redirects (Breaking change) 836 837 The default for `images.maximumRedirects` has changed from unlimited to 3 redirects maximum. 838 839 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 840 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 841 842 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 843 images: { 844 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 845 // or 846 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 847 }, 848 } 849 850 export default nextConfig 851 ``` 852 853 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 854 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 855 const nextConfig = { 856 images: { 857 maximumRedirects: 0, // Disable redirects 858 // or 859 maximumRedirects: 5, // Increase for edge cases 860 }, 861 } 862 863 module.exports = nextConfig 864 ``` 865 866 ### `next/legacy/image` Component (deprecated) 867 868 The `next/legacy/image` component is deprecated. Use `next/image` instead: 869 870 ```tsx 871 // Before 872 import Image from 'next/legacy/image' 873 874 // After 875 import Image from 'next/image' 876 ``` 877 878 ### `images.domains` Configuration (deprecated) 879 880 The `images.domains` config is deprecated. 881 882 ```js filename="next.config.js" 883 // image.domains is deprecated 884 module.exports = { 885 images: { 886 domains: ['example.com'], 887 }, 888 } 889 ``` 890 891 Use `images.remotePatterns` instead for improved security: 892 893 ```js filename="next.config.js" 894 // Use image.remotePatterns instead 895 module.exports = { 896 images: { 897 remotePatterns: [ 898 { 899 protocol: 'https', 900 hostname: 'example.com', 901 }, 902 ], 903 }, 904 } 905 ``` 906 907 ## Concurrent `dev` and `build` 908 909 `next dev` and `next build` now use separate output directories, enabling concurrent execution. The `next dev` command outputs to `.next/dev`. 910 911 Additionally, a lockfile mechanism prevents multiple `next dev` or `next build` instances on the same project. 912 913 The [Turbopack tracing command](/docs/app/guides/local-development#turbopack-tracing) should be: 914 915 ```bash package="pnpm" 916 pnpm next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 917 ``` 918 919 ```bash package="npm" 920 npx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 921 ``` 922 923 ```bash package="yarn" 924 yarn next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 925 ``` 926 927 ```bash package="bun" 928 bunx next internal trace .next-profiles/trace-turbopack.bin 929 ``` 930 931 ## Parallel Routes `default.js` requirement 932 933 All [parallel route](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/parallel-routes) slots now require explicit `default.js` files. Builds will fail without them. 934 935 To maintain previous behavior, create a [`default.js`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/default) file that calls `notFound()` or returns `null`. 936 937 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 938 import { notFound } from 'next/navigation' 939 940 export default function Default() { 941 notFound() 942 } 943 ``` 944 945 Or return `null`: 946 947 ```tsx filename="app/@modal/default.tsx" 948 export default function Default() { 949 return null 950 } 951 ``` 952 953 ## ESLint Flat Config 954 955 `@next/eslint-plugin-next` now defaults to ESLint Flat Config format, aligning with ESLint v10 which will drop legacy config support. 956 957 Make sure to review our API reference for the [`@next/eslint-plugin-next`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/eslint#setup-eslint) plugin. 958 959 If you're using the legacy `.eslintrc` format, consider migrating to the flat config format. See the [ESLint migration guide](https://eslint.org/docs/latest/use/configure/migration-guide) for details. 960 961 ## Scroll Behavior Override 962 963 In **previous versions of Next.js**, if you had set `scroll-behavior: smooth` globally on your `` element via CSS, Next.js would override this during SPA route transitions, as follows: 964 965 1. Temporarily set `scroll-behavior` to `auto` 966 2. Perform the navigation (causing instant scroll to top) 967 3. Restore your original `scroll-behavior` value 968 969 This ensured that page navigation always felt snappy and instant, even when you had smooth scrolling enabled for in-page navigation. However, this manipulation could be expensive, especially at the start of every navigation. 970 971 In **Next.js 16**, this behavior has changed. By default, Next.js will **no longer override** your `scroll-behavior` setting during navigation. 972 973 **If you want Next.js to perform this override** (the previous default behavior), add the `data-scroll-behavior="smooth"` attribute to your `` element: 974 975 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" 976 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 977 return ( 978 979 {children} 980 981 ) 982 } 983 ``` 984 985 ## Performance Improvements 986 987 Significant performance optimizations for `next dev` and `next start` commands, along with improved terminal output with clearer formatting, better error messages, and improved performance metrics. 988 989 **Next.js 16** removes the `size` and `First Load JS` metrics from the `next build` output. We found these to be inaccurate in server-driven architectures using React Server Components. Both our Turbopack and Webpack implementations had issues, and disagreed on how to account for Client Components payload. 990 991 The most effective way to measure actual route performance is through tools such as [Chrome Lighthouse](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/overview) or Vercel Analytics, which focus on Core Web Vitals and downloaded resource sizes. 992 993 ### `next dev` config load 994 995 In previous versions the Next config file was loaded twice during development: 996 997 - When running the `next dev` command 998 - When the `next dev` command started the Next.js server 999 1000 This was inefficient because the `next dev` command doesn't need the config file to start the Next.js server. 1001 1002 A consequence of this change is that, when running `next dev` checking if `process.argv` includes `'dev'`, in your Next.js config file, will return `false`. 1003 1004 > **Good to know**: The `typegen`, and `build` commands, are still visible in `process.argv`. 1005 1006 This is specially important for plugins that trigger side-effects on `next dev`. If that's the case, it might be enough to check if `NODE_ENV` is set to `development`. 1007 1008 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1009 import { startServer } from 'docs-lib/dev-server' 1010 1011 const isDev = process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' 1012 1013 if (isDev) { 1014 startServer() 1015 } 1016 1017 const nextConfig = { 1018 /* Your config options */ 1019 } 1020 1021 module.exports = nextConfig 1022 ``` 1023 1024 Alternatively, use the [`phase`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js#phase) in which the configuration is loaded. 1025 1026 ## Build Adapters API (alpha) 1027 1028 Following the [Build Adapters RFC](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/discussions/77740), the first alpha version of the Build Adapters API is now available. 1029 1030 Build Adapters allow you to create custom adapters that hook into the build process, enabling deployment platforms and custom build integrations to modify Next.js configuration or process build output. 1031 1032 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1033 const nextConfig = { 1034 experimental: { 1035 adapterPath: require.resolve('./my-adapter.js'), 1036 }, 1037 } 1038 1039 module.exports = nextConfig 1040 ``` 1041 1042 `adapterPath` was promoted to a stable, top-level option in 16.2.0. See [`adapterPath`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/adapterPath) for the current API reference. 1043 1044 ## Modern Sass API 1045 1046 `sass-loader` has been bumped to v16, which supports [modern Sass syntax](https://sass-lang.com/documentation/js-api/#md:usage) and new features. 1047 1048 ## Removals 1049 1050 These features were previously deprecated and are now removed: 1051 1052 ### AMP Support 1053 1054 AMP adoption has declined significantly, and maintaining this feature adds complexity to the framework. All AMP APIs and configurations have been removed: 1055 1056 - `amp` configuration from your Next config file 1057 - `next/amp` hook imports and usage (`useAmp`) 1058 1059 ```tsx 1060 // Removed 1061 import { useAmp } from 'next/amp' 1062 1063 // Removed 1064 export const config = { amp: true } 1065 ``` 1066 1067 - `export const config = { amp: true }` from pages 1068 1069 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1070 const nextConfig = { 1071 // Removed 1072 amp: { 1073 canonicalBase: 'https://example.com', 1074 }, 1075 } 1076 1077 module.exports = nextConfig 1078 ``` 1079 1080 Evaluate if AMP is still necessary for your use case. Most performance benefits can now be achieved through Next.js's built-in optimizations and modern web standards. 1081 1082 ### `next lint` Command 1083 1084 The `next lint` command has been removed. Use Biome or ESLint directly. `next build` no longer runs linting. 1085 1086 A codemod is available to automate migration: 1087 1088 ```bash package="pnpm" 1089 pnpm dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1090 ``` 1091 1092 ```bash package="npm" 1093 npx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1094 ``` 1095 1096 ```bash package="yarn" 1097 yarn dlx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1098 ``` 1099 1100 ```bash package="bun" 1101 bunx @next/codemod@canary next-lint-to-eslint-cli . 1102 ``` 1103 1104 The `eslint` option in the Next.js config file is also removed. 1105 1106 ```js filename="next.config.mjs" 1107 /** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */ 1108 const nextConfig = { 1109 // No longer supported 1110 // eslint: {}, 1111 } 1112 1113 export default nextConfig 1114 ``` 1115 1116 ### Runtime Configuration 1117 1118 `serverRuntimeConfig` and `publicRuntimeConfig` have been removed. Use environment variables instead. 1119 1120 **Before (Next.js 15):** 1121 1122 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1123 module.exports = { 1124 serverRuntimeConfig: { 1125 dbUrl: process.env.DATABASE_URL, 1126 }, 1127 publicRuntimeConfig: { 1128 apiUrl: '/api', 1129 }, 1130 } 1131 ``` 1132 1133 ```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" 1134 import getConfig from 'next/config' 1135 1136 export default function Page() { 1137 const { publicRuntimeConfig } = getConfig() 1138 return

API URL: {publicRuntimeConfig.apiUrl}

1139 } 1140 ``` 1141 1142 **After (Next.js 16):** 1143 1144 For server-only values, access environment variables directly in Server Components: 1145 1146 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1147 async function fetchData() { 1148 const dbUrl = process.env.DATABASE_URL 1149 // Use for server-side operations only 1150 return await db.query(dbUrl, 'SELECT * FROM users') 1151 } 1152 1153 export default async function Page() { 1154 const data = await fetchData() 1155 return
{/* render data */}
1156 } 1157 ``` 1158 1159 > **Good to know**: Use the [taint API](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/taint) to prevent accidentally passing sensitive server values to Client Components. 1160 1161 For client-accessible values, use the `NEXT_PUBLIC_` prefix: 1162 1163 ```bash filename=".env.local" 1164 NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL="/api" 1165 ``` 1166 1167 ```tsx filename="app/components/client-component.tsx" 1168 'use client' 1169 1170 export default function ClientComponent() { 1171 const apiUrl = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL 1172 return

1173 } 1174 ``` 1175 1176 To ensure environment variables are read at runtime (not bundled at build time), use the [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection) function before reading from `process.env`: 1177 1178 ```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" 1179 import { connection } from 'next/server' 1180 1181 export default async function Page() { 1182 await connection() 1183 const config = process.env.RUNTIME_CONFIG 1184 return

{config}

1185 } 1186 ``` 1187 1188 Learn more about [environment variables](/docs/app/guides/environment-variables). 1189 1190 ### `devIndicators` Options 1191 1192 The following options have been removed from [`devIndicators`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/devIndicators): 1193 1194 - `appIsrStatus` 1195 - `buildActivity` 1196 - `buildActivityPosition` 1197 1198 The indicator itself remains available. 1199 1200 ### `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` 1201 1202 The `experimental.dynamicIO` and `experimental.useCache` flags have been removed. 1203 1204 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1205 // Before: experimental.useCache 1206 module.exports = { 1207 experimental: { 1208 useCache: true, 1209 }, 1210 } 1211 ``` 1212 1213 ```js filename="next.config.js" 1214 // Before: experimental.dynamicIO 1215 module.exports = { 1216 experimental: { 1217 dynamicIO: true, 1218 }, 1219 } 1220 ``` 1221 1222 If you were actively using these flags, migrate to top-level [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents): 1223 1224 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 1225 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 1226 1227 // After 1228 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 1229 cacheComponents: true, 1230 } 1231 1232 export default nextConfig 1233 ``` 1234 1235 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 1236 // After 1237 module.exports = { 1238 cacheComponents: true, 1239 } 1240 ``` 1241 1242 If you were not actively adopting Cache Components, remove the flags instead. You can create a page by default exporting a component from the file: 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 9 export default function Page({ 10 params, 11 searchParams, 12 }: { 13 params: Promise<{ slug: string }> 14 searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 15 }) { 16 return

My Page

17 } 18 ``` 19 20 ```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher 21 export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) { 22 return

My Page

23 } 24 ``` 25 26 ## Good to know 27 28 - The `.js`, `.jsx`, or `.tsx` file extensions can be used for `page`. 29 - A `page` is always the **leaf** of the route subtree. 30 - A `page` file is required to make a route segment **publicly accessible**. 31 - Pages are [Server Components](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/server-components) by default, but can be set to a [Client Component](https://react.dev/reference/rsc/use-client). 32 - In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `page.js` is the innermost file convention. It is wrapped by `loading.js` (Suspense boundary), `error.js` (error boundary), `template.js`, and `layout.js` in the same segment. 33 34 ## Reference 35 36 ### Props 37 38 #### `params` (optional) 39 40 A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) from the root segment down to that page. 41 42 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher 43 export default async function Page({ 44 params, 45 }: { 46 params: Promise<{ slug: string }> 47 }) { 48 const { slug } = await params 49 } 50 ``` 51 52 ```jsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.js" switcher 53 export default async function Page({ params }) { 54 const { slug } = await params 55 } 56 ``` 57 58 | Example Route | URL | `params` | 59 | ------------------------------------ | ----------- | --------------------------------------- | 60 | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js` | `/shop/1` | `Promise<{ slug: '1' }>` | 61 | `app/shop/[category]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ category: '1', item: '2' }>` | 62 | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>` | 63 64 - Since the `params` prop is a promise, you must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values. 65 - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 66 67 #### `searchParams` (optional) 68 69 A promise that resolves to an object containing the [search parameters](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters) of the current URL. For example: 70 71 ```tsx filename="app/shop/page.tsx" switcher 72 export default async function Page({ 73 searchParams, 74 }: { 75 searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 76 }) { 77 const filters = (await searchParams).filters 78 } 79 ``` 80 81 ```jsx filename="app/shop/page.js" switcher 82 export default async function Page({ searchParams }) { 83 const filters = (await searchParams).filters 84 } 85 ``` 86 87 Client Component **pages** can also access `searchParams` using React’s [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) hook: 88 89 ```tsx filename="app/shop/page.tsx" switcher 90 'use client' 91 import { use } from 'react' 92 93 export default function Page({ 94 searchParams, 95 }: { 96 searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }> 97 }) { 98 const filters = use(searchParams).filters 99 } 100 ``` 101 102 ```jsx filename="app/page.jsx" switcher 103 'use client' 104 import { use } from 'react' 105 106 export default function Page({ searchParams }) { 107 const filters = use(searchParams).filters 108 } 109 ``` 110 111 | Example URL | `searchParams` | 112 | --------------- | ----------------------------- | 113 | `/shop?a=1` | `Promise<{ a: '1' }>` | 114 | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `Promise<{ a: '1', b: '2' }>` | 115 | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `Promise<{ a: ['1', '2'] }>` | 116 117 - Since the `searchParams` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values. 118 - In version 14 and earlier, `searchParams` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 119 - `searchParams` is a **[Request-time API](/docs/app/glossary#request-time-apis)** whose values cannot be known ahead of time. Using it will opt the page into **[dynamic rendering](/docs/app/glossary#dynamic-rendering)** at request time. 120 - With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), where you access `searchParams` in the component tree determines how much of the page can be prerendered. See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell). 121 - `searchParams` is a plain JavaScript object, not a `URLSearchParams` instance. 122 123 ### Page Props Helper 124 125 You can type pages with `PageProps` to get strongly typed `params` and `searchParams` from the route literal. `PageProps` is a globally available helper. 126 127 ```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" 128 export default async function Page(props: PageProps<'/blog/[slug]'>) { 129 const { slug } = await props.params 130 const query = await props.searchParams 131 return

1	---
2	title: generateStaticParams
3	description: API reference for the generateStaticParams function.
4	---
5	
6	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7	
8	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9	
10	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
16	export async function generateStaticParams() {
17	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
18	
19	  return posts.map((post) => ({
20	    slug: post.slug,
21	  }))
22	}
23	
24	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
25	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
26	export default async function Page({
27	  params,
28	}: {
29	  params: Promise<{ slug: string }>
30	}) {
31	  const { slug } = await params
32	  // ...
33	}
34	```
35	
36	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
37	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment
38	export async function generateStaticParams() {
39	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
40	
41	  return posts.map((post) => ({
42	    slug: post.slug,
43	  }))
44	}
45	
46	// Multiple versions of this page will be statically generated
47	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
48	export default async function Page({ params }) {
49	  const { slug } = await params
50	  // ...
51	}
52	```
53	
54	> **Good to know**:
55	>
56	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.
62	
63	## Parameters
64	
65	`options.params` (optional)
66	
67	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68	
69	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70	
71	## Returns
72	
73	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.
74	
75	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
76	- The properties name is the segment's name, and the properties value is what that segment should be filled in with.
77	
78	| Example Route                    | `generateStaticParams` Return Type        |
79	| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
80	| `/product/[id]`                  | `{ id: string }[]`                        |
81	| `/products/[category]/[product]` | `{ category: string, product: string }[]` |
82	| `/products/[...slug]`            | `{ slug: string[] }[]`                    |
83	
84	## Single Dynamic Segment
85	
86	```tsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
87	export function generateStaticParams() {
88	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
89	}
90	
91	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
92	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
93	// - /product/1
94	// - /product/2
95	// - /product/3
96	export default async function Page({
97	  params,
98	}: {
99	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
100	}) {
101	  const { id } = await params
102	  // ...
103	}
104	```
105	
106	```jsx filename="app/product/[id]/page.js" switcher
107	export function generateStaticParams() {
108	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
109	}
110	
111	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
112	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
113	// - /product/1
114	// - /product/2
115	// - /product/3
116	export default async function Page({ params }) {
117	  const { id } = await params
118	  // ...
119	}
120	```
121	
122	## Multiple Dynamic Segments
123	
124	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
125	export function generateStaticParams() {
126	  return [
127	    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
128	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
129	    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
130	  ]
131	}
132	
133	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
134	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
135	// - /products/a/1
136	// - /products/b/2
137	// - /products/c/3
138	export default async function Page({
139	  params,
140	}: {
141	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
142	}) {
143	  const { category, product } = await params
144	  // ...
145	}
146	```
147	
148	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
149	export function generateStaticParams() {
150	  return [
151	    { category: 'a', product: '1' },
152	    { category: 'b', product: '2' },
153	    { category: 'c', product: '3' },
154	  ]
155	}
156	
157	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
158	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
159	// - /products/a/1
160	// - /products/b/2
161	// - /products/c/3
162	export default async function Page({ params }) {

164	  // ...
165	}

167	
168	## Catch-all Dynamic Segment
169	
170	```tsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.tsx" switcher
171	export function generateStaticParams() {
172	  return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
173	}
174	
175	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
176	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
177	// - /product/a/1
178	// - /product/b/2
179	// - /product/c/3
180	export default async function Page({
181	  params,
182	}: {
183	  params: Promise<{ slug: string[] }>
184	}) {
185	  const { slug } = await params
186	  // ...
187	}
188	```
189	
190	```jsx filename="app/product/[...slug]/page.js" switcher
191	export function generateStaticParams() {
192	  return [{ slug: ['a', '1'] }, { slug: ['b', '2'] }, { slug: ['c', '3'] }]
193	}
194	
195	// Three versions of this page will be statically generated
196	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`
197	// - /product/a/1
198	// - /product/b/2
199	// - /product/c/3
200	export default async function Page({ params }) {
201	  const { slug } = await params
202	  // ...
203	}
204	```
205	
206	## Examples
207	
208	### Prerendering
209	
210	#### All paths at build time
211	
212	To statically render all paths at build time, supply the full list of paths to `generateStaticParams`:
213	
214	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
215	export async function generateStaticParams() {
216	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
217	
218	  return posts.map((post) => ({
219	    slug: post.slug,
220	  }))
221	}
222	```
223	
224	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
225	export async function generateStaticParams() {
226	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
227	
228	  return posts.map((post) => ({
229	    slug: post.slug,
230	  }))
231	}
232	```
233	
234	#### Subset of paths at build time
235	
236	To statically render a subset of paths at build time, and the rest the first time they're visited at runtime, return a partial list of paths:
237	
238	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
239	export async function generateStaticParams() {
240	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
241	
242	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
243	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
244	    slug: post.slug,
245	  }))
246	}
247	```
248	
249	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
250	export async function generateStaticParams() {
251	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
252	
253	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
254	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
255	    slug: post.slug,
256	  }))
257	}
258	```
259	
260	Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
261	
262	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
263	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
264	export const dynamicParams = false
265	
266	export async function generateStaticParams() {
267	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
268	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
269	
270	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
271	    slug: post.slug,
272	  }))
273	}
274	```
275	
276	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
277	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
278	export const dynamicParams = false
279	
280	export async function generateStaticParams() {
281	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
282	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
283	
284	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
285	    slug: post.slug,
286	  }))
287	}
288	```
289	
290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
295	export async function generateStaticParams() {
296	  return []
297	}
298	```
299	
300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
315	
316	### With Route Handlers
317	
318	You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
319	
320	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
321	export async function generateStaticParams() {
322	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
323	}
324	
325	export async function GET(
326	  request: Request,
327	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
328	) {
329	  const { id } = await params
330	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
331	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
332	}
333	```
334	
335	```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
336	export async function generateStaticParams() {
337	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
338	}
339	
340	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
341	  const { id } = await params
342	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
343	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
344	}
345	```
346	
347	### Route Handlers with Cache Components
348	
349	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
350	
351	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
352	export async function generateStaticParams() {
353	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
354	}
355	
356	async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
357	  'use cache'
358	  const resolvedId = await id
359	  const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
360	  return response.json()
361	}
362	
363	export async function GET(
364	  request: Request,
365	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
366	) {
367	  const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
368	  return Response.json(post)
369	}
370	```
371	
372	See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
373	
374	### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
375	
376	To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
377	
378	### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
379	
380	You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
381	
382	- `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
383	- `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
384	
385	There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
386	
387	#### Generate params from the bottom up
388	
389	Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
390	
391	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
392	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
393	export async function generateStaticParams() {
394	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
395	
396	  return products.map((product) => ({
397	    category: product.category.slug,
398	    product: product.id,
399	  }))
400	}
401	
402	export default function Page({
403	  params,
404	}: {
405	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
406	}) {
407	  // ...
408	}
409	```
410	
411	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
412	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
413	export async function generateStaticParams() {
414	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
415	
416	  return products.map((product) => ({
417	    category: product.category.slug,
418	    product: product.id,
419	  }))
420	}
421	
422	export default function Page({ params }) {
423	  // ...
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Generate params from the top down
428	
429	Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
430	
431	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
432	// Generate segments for [category]
433	export async function generateStaticParams() {
434	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
435	
436	  return products.map((product) => ({
437	    category: product.category.slug,
438	  }))
439	}
440	
441	export default function Layout({
442	  params,
443	}: {
444	  params: Promise<{ category: string }>
445	}) {
446	  // ...
447	}
448	```
449	
450	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
451	// Generate segments for [category]
452	export async function generateStaticParams() {
453	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
454	
455	  return products.map((product) => ({
456	    category: product.category.slug,
457	  }))
458	}
459	
460	export default function Layout({ params }) {
461	  // ...
462	}
463	```
464	
465	A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
466	
467	The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
468	
469	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
470	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
471	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
472	export async function generateStaticParams({
473	  params: { category },
474	}: {
475	  params: { category: string }
476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
490	}) {
491	  // ...
492	}
493	```
494	
495	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
496	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
498	export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
499	  const products = await fetch(
500	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
501	  ).then((res) => res.json())
502	
503	  return products.map((product) => ({
504	    product: product.id,
505	  }))
506	}
507	
508	export default function Page({ params }) {
509	  // ...
510	}
511	```
512	
513	Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
514	
515	> **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
516	
517	For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
518	
519	```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
520	export async function generateStaticParams({
521	  params: { category },
522	}: {
523	  params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
524	}) {
525	  const products = await fetch(
526	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
527	  ).then((res) => res.json())
528	
529	  return products.map((product) => ({
530	    product: product.id,
531	  }))
532	}
533	```
534	
535	> **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
536	
537	## Version History
538	
539	| Version   | Changes                            |
540	| --------- | ---------------------------------- |
541	| `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

5	
6	The `generateStaticParams` function can be used in combination with [dynamic route segments](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) to [**statically generate**](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering) routes at build time instead of on-demand at request time.
7	
8	`generateStaticParams` can be used with:
9	
10	- [Pages](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (`page.tsx`/`page.js`)
11	- [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) (`layout.tsx`/`layout.js`)
12	- [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) (`route.ts`/`route.js`)
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
15	// Return a list of `params` to populate the [slug] dynamic segment

18

21	  }))
22	}

25	// using the `params` returned by `generateStaticParams`

27	  params,
28	}: {

30	}) {

32	  // ...
33	}
34	```

54	> **Good to know**:
55	>
56	> - You can use the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option to control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
57	> - You must return [an empty array from `generateStaticParams`](#all-paths-at-runtime) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic) in order to revalidate (ISR) [paths at runtime](#all-paths-at-runtime).
58	> - During `next dev`, `generateStaticParams` will be called when you navigate to a route.
59	> - During `next build`, `generateStaticParams` runs before the corresponding Layouts or Pages are generated.
60	> - During revalidation (ISR), `generateStaticParams` will not be called again.
61	> - `generateStaticParams` replaces the [`getStaticPaths`](/docs/pages/api-reference/functions/get-static-paths) function in the Pages Router.

63	## Parameters
64	
65	`options.params` (optional)
66	
67	If multiple dynamic segments in a route use `generateStaticParams`, the child `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each set of `params` the parent generates.
68	
69	The `params` object contains the populated `params` from the parent `generateStaticParams`, which can be used to [generate the `params` in a child segment](#multiple-dynamic-segments-in-a-route).
70

72	
73	`generateStaticParams` should return an array of objects where each object represents the populated dynamic segments of a single route.

75	- Each property in the object is a dynamic segment to be filled in for the route.
