249	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
250	export async function generateStaticParams() {
251	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
252	
253	  // Render the first 10 posts at build time
254	  return posts.slice(0, 10).map((post) => ({
255	    slug: post.slug,
256	  }))
257	}
258	```
259	
260	Then, by using the [`dynamicParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/dynamicParams) segment config option, you can control what happens when a dynamic segment is visited that was not generated with `generateStaticParams`.
261	
262	```tsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx" switcher
263	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
264	export const dynamicParams = false
265	
266	export async function generateStaticParams() {
267	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
268	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
269	
270	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
271	    slug: post.slug,
272	  }))
273	}
274	```
275	
276	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js" switcher
277	// All posts besides the top 10 will be a 404
278	export const dynamicParams = false
279	
280	export async function generateStaticParams() {
281	  const posts = await fetch('https://.../posts').then((res) => res.json())
282	  const topPosts = posts.slice(0, 10)
283	
284	  return topPosts.map((post) => ({
285	    slug: post.slug,
286	  }))
287	}
288	```
289	
290	#### All paths at runtime
291	
292	To statically render all paths the first time they're visited, return an empty array (no paths will be rendered at build time) or utilize [`export const dynamic = 'force-static'`](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components#dynamic):
293	
294	```jsx filename="app/blog/[slug]/page.js"
295	export async function generateStaticParams() {
296	  return []
297	}
298	```
299	
300	> **Good to know:**
301	>
302	> - You must always return an array from `generateStaticParams`, even if it's empty. Otherwise, the route will be dynamically rendered.
303	
304	```jsx filename="app/changelog/[slug]/page.js"
305	export const dynamic = 'force-static'
306	```
307	
308	#### With Cache Components
309	
310	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with dynamic routes, `generateStaticParams` must return **at least one param**. Empty arrays cause a [build error](/docs/messages/empty-generate-static-params). This allows Cache Components to validate your route doesn't incorrectly access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or `searchParams` at runtime.
311	
312	> **Good to know**: If you don't know the actual param values at build time, you can return a placeholder param (e.g., `[{ slug: '__placeholder__' }]`) for validation, then handle it in your page with `notFound()`. However, this prevents build time validation from working effectively and may cause runtime errors.
313	
314	See the [dynamic routes section](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#with-cache-components) for detailed walkthroughs, or [ISR with Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/incremental-static-regeneration-cache-components) for prerendering a subset of routes and serving App Shells for the rest.
315	
316	### With Route Handlers
317	
318	You can use `generateStaticParams` with [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route) to statically generate API responses at build time:
319	
320	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts" switcher
321	export async function generateStaticParams() {
322	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
323	}
324	
325	export async function GET(
326	  request: Request,
327	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
328	) {
329	  const { id } = await params
330	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
331	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
332	}
333	```
334	
335	```js filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.js" switcher
336	export async function generateStaticParams() {
337	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
338	}
339	
340	export async function GET(request, { params }) {
341	  const { id } = await params
342	  // This will be statically generated for IDs 1, 2, and 3
343	  return Response.json({ id, title: `Post ${id}` })
344	}
345	```
346	
347	### Route Handlers with Cache Components
348	
349	When using [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching), combine with `use cache` for optimal caching:
350	
351	```ts filename="app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts"
352	export async function generateStaticParams() {
353	  return [{ id: '1' }, { id: '2' }, { id: '3' }]
354	}
355	
356	async function getPost(id: Promise<string>) {
357	  'use cache'
358	  const resolvedId = await id
359	  const response = await fetch(`https://api.example.com/posts/${resolvedId}`)
360	  return response.json()
361	}
362	
363	export async function GET(
364	  request: Request,
365	  { params }: RouteContext<'/api/posts/[id]'>
366	) {
367	  const post = await getPost(params.then((p) => p.id))
368	  return Response.json(post)
369	}
370	```
371	
372	See the [Route Handlers documentation](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route#static-generation-with-generatestaticparams) for more details.
373	
374	### Disable rendering for unspecified paths
375	
376	To prevent unspecified paths from being prerendered at runtime, add the `export const dynamicParams = false` option in a route segment. When this config option is used, only paths provided by `generateStaticParams` will be served, and unspecified routes will 404 or match (in the case of [catch-all routes](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes#catch-all-segments)).
377	
378	### Multiple Dynamic Segments in a Route
379	
380	You can generate params for dynamic segments above the current layout or page, but **not below**. For example, given the `app/products/[category]/[product]` route:
381	
382	- `app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js` can generate params for **both** `[category]` and `[product]`.
383	- `app/products/[category]/layout.js` can **only** generate params for `[category]`.
384	
385	There are two approaches to generating params for a route with multiple dynamic segments:
386	
387	#### Generate params from the bottom up
388	
389	Generate multiple dynamic segments from the child route segment.
390	
391	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
392	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
393	export async function generateStaticParams() {
394	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
395	
396	  return products.map((product) => ({
397	    category: product.category.slug,
398	    product: product.id,
399	  }))
400	}
401	
402	export default function Page({
403	  params,
404	}: {
405	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
406	}) {
407	  // ...
408	}
409	```
410	
411	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
412	// Generate segments for both [category] and [product]
413	export async function generateStaticParams() {
414	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
415	
416	  return products.map((product) => ({
417	    category: product.category.slug,
418	    product: product.id,
419	  }))
420	}
421	
422	export default function Page({ params }) {
423	  // ...
424	}
425	```
426	
427	#### Generate params from the top down
428	
429	Generate the parent segments first and use the result to generate the child segments.
430	
431	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.tsx" switcher
432	// Generate segments for [category]
433	export async function generateStaticParams() {
434	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
435	
436	  return products.map((product) => ({
437	    category: product.category.slug,
438	  }))
439	}
440	
441	export default function Layout({
442	  params,
443	}: {
444	  params: Promise<{ category: string }>
445	}) {
446	  // ...
447	}
448	```
449	
450	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/layout.js" switcher
451	// Generate segments for [category]
452	export async function generateStaticParams() {
453	  const products = await fetch('https://.../products').then((res) => res.json())
454	
455	  return products.map((product) => ({
456	    category: product.category.slug,
457	  }))
458	}
459	
460	export default function Layout({ params }) {
461	  // ...
462	}
463	```
464	
465	A child route segment's `generateStaticParams` function is executed once for each segment a parent `generateStaticParams` generates.
466	
467	The child `generateStaticParams` function can use the `params` returned from the parent `generateStaticParams` function to dynamically generate its own segments.
468	
469	```tsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
470	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
471	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
472	export async function generateStaticParams({
473	  params: { category },
474	}: {
475	  params: { category: string }
476	}) {
477	  const products = await fetch(
478	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
479	  ).then((res) => res.json())
480	
481	  return products.map((product) => ({
482	    product: product.id,
483	  }))
484	}
485	
486	export default function Page({
487	  params,
488	}: {
489	  params: Promise<{ category: string; product: string }>
490	}) {
491	  // ...
492	}
493	```
494	
495	```jsx filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.js" switcher
496	// Generate segments for [product] using the `params` passed from
497	// the parent segment's `generateStaticParams` function
498	export async function generateStaticParams({ params: { category } }) {
499	  const products = await fetch(
500	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
501	  ).then((res) => res.json())
502	
503	  return products.map((product) => ({
504	    product: product.id,
505	  }))
506	}
507	
508	export default function Page({ params }) {
509	  // ...
510	}
511	```
512	
513	Notice that the params argument can be accessed synchronously and includes only parent segment params.
514	
515	> **Good to know:** When a parent dynamic segment is a [root parameter](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params), you can also read it inside a nested `generateStaticParams` by calling its getter from the `next/root-params` module.
516	
517	For type completion, you can make use of the TypeScript `Awaited` helper in combination with either [`Page Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`Layout Props helper`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper):
518	
519	```ts filename="app/products/[category]/[product]/page.tsx" switcher
520	export async function generateStaticParams({
521	  params: { category },
522	}: {
523	  params: Awaited<LayoutProps<'/products/[category]'>['params']>
524	}) {
525	  const products = await fetch(
526	    `https://.../products?category=${category}`
527	  ).then((res) => res.json())
528	
529	  return products.map((product) => ({
530	    product: product.id,
531	  }))
532	}
533	```
534	
535	> **Good to know**: `fetch` requests are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across all `generate`-prefixed functions, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
536	
537	## Version History
538	
539	| Version   | Changes                            |
540	| --------- | ---------------------------------- |
541	| `v13.0.0` | `generateStaticParams` introduced. |

Below that, a [short lifetime keeps it out of the App Shell](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife#prerendering-behavior), so each navigation fetches it again. 130 131 ### Keeping a route's prefetch static 132 133 When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies), [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), `params`, and `searchParams` sits below `unstable_navigation()`, the prerender a prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the prefetch is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a link into the route costs no server CPU at all. 134 135 ```tsx filename="app/feed/page.tsx" highlight={17} 136 import { Suspense } from 'react' 137 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 138 import { unstable_navigation } from 'next/cache' 139 140 export default function Page() { 141 return ( 142 <> 143 {/* static, and so is the whole prefetch */} 144 Loading stories...

}> 145 146 147 148 ) 149 } 150 151 async function Stories() { 152 await unstable_navigation() 153 const topic = (await cookies()).get('topic')?.value ?? 'all' 154 return 155 } 156 ``` 157 158 ## Good to know 159 160 - The function has no effect on the initial load of a page. 161 - Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), it does not mark the subtree as request-dependent. Content below `await unstable_navigation()` stays fully cacheable and can be wrapped in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache). It also keeps its cache lifetime. 162 - Reading `cookies()` or `headers()` below `unstable_navigation()` does not make the route's prefetches render per request, so they can still be served from static output. Those accesses are ignored, because they would not have resolved in a prefetch either. 163 - A call outside a `` boundary surfaces a validation insight in development. It is reported even on a page that is currently prerendered in full, because the same page starts deferring content as soon as it switches to a runtime shell. 164 - Calling it inside `use cache`, `use cache: private`, [`unstable_cache()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unstable_cache), [`after()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/after), [`generateStaticParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-static-params), or a Client Component throws. 165 166 {/* TODO: link the validation insight error page from the bullet above once it merges. */} 167 168 ## Reference 169 170 ### Type 171 172 ```ts 173 function unstable_navigation(): Promise 174 ``` 175 176 ### Parameters 177 178 - The function does not accept any parameters. 179 180 ### Returns 181 182 A `Promise`. It is not meant to be consumed. 183 184 ## Version History 185 186 | Version | Changes | 187 | --------- | ---------------------------- | 188 | `v16.4.0` | `unstable_navigation` added. | 189

1	---
2	title: generateMetadata
3	description: Learn how to add Metadata to your Next.js application for improved search engine optimization (SEO) and web shareability.
4	related:
5	  title: Next Steps
6	  description: View all the Metadata API options.
7	  links:
8	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata
9	    - app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport
10	    - app/getting-started/caching
11	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
12	---
13	
14	You can use the `metadata` object or the `generateMetadata` function to define metadata.
15	
16	## The `metadata` object
17	
18	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
19	
20	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
21	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
22	
23	export const metadata: Metadata = {
24	  title: '...',
25	  description: '...',
26	}
27	
28	export default function Page() {}
29	```
30	
31	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
32	export const metadata = {
33	  title: '...',
34	  description: '...',
35	}
36	
37	export default function Page() {}
38	```
39	
40	> See the [Metadata Fields](#metadata-fields) for a complete list of supported options.
41	
42	## `generateMetadata` function
43	
44	Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
45	
46	Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
47	
48	Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
51	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
52	
53	type Props = {
54	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
55	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
56	}
57	
58	export async function generateMetadata(
59	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
60	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
61	): Promise<Metadata> {
62	  // read route params
63	  const { id } = await params
64	
65	  // fetch data
66	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
67	
68	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
69	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
70	
71	  return {
72	    title: product.title,
73	    openGraph: {
74	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
80	```
81	
82	```jsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.js" switcher
83	export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }, parent) {
84	  // read route params
85	  const { id } = await params
86	
87	  // fetch data
88	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
89	
90	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
91	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
92	
93	  return {
94	    title: product.title,
95	    openGraph: {
96	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
97	    },
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {}
102	```
103	
104	For type completion of `params` and `searchParams`, you can type the first argument with [`PageProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`LayoutProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) for pages and layouts respectively.
105	
106	> **Good to know**:
107	>
108	> - Metadata can be added to `layout.js` and `page.js` files.
109	> - Next.js will automatically resolve the metadata, and create the relevant `<head>` tags for the page.
110	> - The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are **only supported in Server Components**.
111	> - You cannot export both the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function from the same route segment.
112	> - `fetch` requests inside `generateMetadata` are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components.
113	> - React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
114	> - [File-based metadata](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) has the higher priority and will override the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function.
115	
116	## Why `generateMetadata` is Server Component only
117	
118	`generateMetadata` and the `metadata` export are only supported in Server Components because metadata must be resolved on the server before the page component is rendered. This allows Next.js to include the metadata in the initial HTML response.
119	
120	If you need to use Client Component features, keep your `page.tsx` as a Server Component and move the Client Component logic to a separate file:
121	
122	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
123	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
124	import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
125	
126	export const metadata: Metadata = {
127	  title: 'My Page',
128	}
129	
130	export default function Page() {
131	  return <InteractiveComponent />
132	}
133	```
134	
135	```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
136	import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
137	
138	export const metadata = {
139	  title: 'My Page',
140	}
141	
142	export default function Page() {
143	  return <InteractiveComponent />
144	}
145	```
146	
147	```tsx filename="app/interactive-component.tsx" switcher
148	'use client'
149	
150	export function InteractiveComponent() {
151	  // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```jsx filename="app/interactive-component.js" switcher
156	'use client'
157	
158	export function InteractiveComponent() {
159	  // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
160	}
161	```
162	
163	## Reference
164	
165	### Parameters
166	
167	`generateMetadata` function accepts the following parameters:
168	
169	- `props` - An object containing the parameters of the current route:
170	  - `params` - An object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to the segment `generateMetadata` is called from. Examples:
171	
172	    | Route                           | URL         | `params`                  |
173	    | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
174	    | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
175	    | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
176	    | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |
177	
178	  - `searchParams` - An object containing the current URL's [search params](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters). Examples:
179	
180	    | URL             | `searchParams`       |
181	    | --------------- | -------------------- |
182	    | `/shop?a=1`     | `{ a: '1' }`         |
183	    | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `{ a: '1', b: '2' }` |
184	    | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `{ a: ['1', '2'] }`  |
185	
186	- `parent` - A promise of the resolved metadata from parent route segments.
187	
188	### Returns
189	
190	`generateMetadata` should return a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) containing one or more metadata fields.
191	
192	> **Good to know**:
193	>
194	> - If metadata doesn't depend on request information, it should be defined using the static [`metadata` object](#the-metadata-object) rather than `generateMetadata`.
195	> - `fetch` requests are automatically memoized for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
196	> - `searchParams` are only available in `page.js` segments.
197	> - The [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) and [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) Next.js methods can also be used inside `generateMetadata`.
198	
199	### Metadata Fields
200	
201	The following fields are supported:
202	
203	#### `title`
204	
205	The `title` attribute is used to set the title of the document. It can be defined as a simple [string](#string) or an optional [template object](#template).
206	
207	##### String
208	
209	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
210	export const metadata = {
211	  title: 'Next.js',
212	}
213	```
214	
215	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
216	<title>Next.js</title>
217	```
218	
219	##### `default`
220	
221	`title.default` can be used to provide a **fallback title** to child route segments that don't define a `title`.
222	
223	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
224	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
225	
226	export const metadata: Metadata = {
227	  title: {
228	    default: 'Acme',
229	  },
230	}
231	```
232	
233	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
234	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
235	
236	export const metadata: Metadata = {}
237	
238	// Output: <title>Acme</title>
239	```
240	
241	##### `template`
242	
243	`title.template` can be used to add a prefix or a suffix to `titles` defined in **child** route segments.
244	
245	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
246	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
247	
248	export const metadata: Metadata = {
249	  title: {
250	    template: '%s | Acme',
251	    default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
252	  },
253	}
254	```
255	
256	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
257	export const metadata = {
258	  title: {
259	    template: '%s | Acme',
260	    default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
261	  },
262	}
263	```
264	
265	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
266	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
267	
268	export const metadata: Metadata = {
269	  title: 'About',
270	}
271	
272	// Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
273	```
274	
275	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
276	export const metadata = {
277	  title: 'About',
278	}
279	
280	// Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
281	```
282	
283	> **Good to know**:
284	>
285	> - `title.template` applies to **child** route segments and **not** the segment it's defined in. This means:
286	>   - `title.default` is **required** when you add a `title.template`.
287	>   - `title.template` defined in `layout.js` will not apply to a `title` defined in a `page.js` of the same route segment.
288	>   - `title.template` defined in `page.js` has no effect because a page is always the terminating segment (it doesn't have any children route segments).
289	> - `title.template` has **no effect** if a route has not defined a `title` or `title.default`.
290	
291	##### `absolute`
292	
293	`title.absolute` can be used to provide a title that **ignores** `title.template` set in parent segments.
294	
295	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
296	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
297	
298	export const metadata: Metadata = {
299	  title: {
300	    template: '%s | Acme',
301	  },
302	}
303	```
304	
305	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
306	export const metadata = {
307	  title: {
308	    template: '%s | Acme',
309	  },
310	}
311	```
312	
313	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
314	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
315	
316	export const metadata: Metadata = {
317	  title: {
318	    absolute: 'About',
319	  },
320	}
321	
322	// Output: <title>About</title>
323	```
324	
325	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
326	export const metadata = {
327	  title: {
328	    absolute: 'About',
329	  },
330	}
331	
332	// Output: <title>About</title>
333	```
334	
335	> **Good to know**:
336	>
337	> - `layout.js`
338	>   - `title` (string) and `title.default` define the default title for child segments (that do not define their own `title`). It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
339	>   - `title.absolute` defines the default title for child segments. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
340	>   - `title.template` defines a new title template for child segments.
341	> - `page.js`
342	>   - If a page does not define its own title the closest parents resolved title will be used.
343	>   - `title` (string) defines the routes title. It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
344	>   - `title.absolute` defines the route title. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
345	>   - `title.template` has no effect in `page.js` because a page is always the terminating segment of a route.
346	
347	### `description`
348	
349	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
350	export const metadata = {
351	  description: 'The React Framework for the Web',
352	}
353	```
354	
355	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
356	<meta name="description" content="The React Framework for the Web" />
357	```
358	
359	### Other fields
360	
361	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
362	export const metadata = {
363	  generator: 'Next.js',
364	  applicationName: 'Next.js',
365	  referrer: 'origin-when-cross-origin',
366	  keywords: ['Next.js', 'React', 'JavaScript'],
367	  authors: [{ name: 'Seb' }, { name: 'Josh', url: 'https://nextjs.org' }],
368	  creator: 'Jiachi Liu',
369	  publisher: 'Sebastian Markbåge',
370	  formatDetection: {
371	    email: false,
372	    address: false,
373	    telephone: false,
374	  },
375	}
376	```
377	
378	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
379	<meta name="application-name" content="Next.js" />
380	<meta name="author" content="Seb" />
381	<link rel="author" href="https://nextjs.org" />
382	<meta name="author" content="Josh" />
383	<meta name="generator" content="Next.js" />
384	<meta name="keywords" content="Next.js,React,JavaScript" />
385	<meta name="referrer" content="origin-when-cross-origin" />
386	<meta name="creator" content="Jiachi Liu" />
387	<meta name="publisher" content="Sebastian Markbåge" />
388	<meta name="format-detection" content="telephone=no, address=no, email=no" />
389	```
390	
391	#### `metadataBase`
392	
393	`metadataBase` is a convenience option to set a base URL prefix for `metadata` fields that require a fully qualified URL.
394	
395	- `metadataBase` allows URL-based `metadata` fields defined in the **current route segment and below** to use a **relative path** instead of an otherwise required absolute URL.
396	- The field's relative path will be composed with `metadataBase` to form a fully qualified URL.
397	
398	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
399	export const metadata = {
400	  metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
401	  alternates: {
402	    canonical: '/',
403	    languages: {
404	      'en-US': '/en-US',
405	      'de-DE': '/de-DE',
406	    },
407	  },
408	  openGraph: {
409	    images: '/og-image.png',
410	  },
411	}
412	```
413	
414	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
415	<link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.com" />
416	<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://acme.com/en-US" />
417	<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-DE" href="https://acme.com/de-DE" />
418	<meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.com/og-image.png" />
419	```
420	
421	> **Good to know**:
422	>
423	> - `metadataBase` is typically set in root `app/layout.js` to apply to URL-based `metadata` fields across all routes.
424	> - When `generateMetadata` uses `'use cache'`, its return value must be serializable. `URL` instances are not supported by Cache Functions, so values such as `metadataBase` should be returned as strings (for example, `url.toString()`). See [`use cache` serialization requirements](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#serialization).
425	> - All URL-based `metadata` fields that require absolute URLs can be configured with a `metadataBase` option.
426	> - `metadataBase` can contain a subdomain e.g. `https://app.acme.com` or base path e.g. `https://acme.com/start/from/here`
427	> - If a `metadata` field provides an absolute URL, `metadataBase` will be ignored.
428	> - Using a relative path in a URL-based `metadata` field without configuring a `metadataBase` will cause a build error.
429	> - Next.js will normalize duplicate slashes between `metadataBase` (e.g. `https://acme.com/`) and a relative field (e.g. `/path`) to a single slash (e.g. `https://acme.com/path`)
430	
431	#### URL Composition
432	
433	URL composition favors developer intent over default directory traversal semantics.
434	
435	- Trailing slashes between `metadataBase` and `metadata` fields are normalized.
436	- An "absolute" path in a `metadata` field (that typically would replace the whole URL path) is treated as a "relative" path (starting from the end of `metadataBase`).
437	
438	For example, given the following `metadataBase`:
439	
440	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
441	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
442	
443	export const metadata: Metadata = {
444	  metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
445	}
446	```
447	
448	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
449	export const metadata = {
450	  metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
451	}
452	```
453	
454	Any `metadata` fields that inherit the above `metadataBase` and set their own value will be resolved as follows:
455	
456	| `metadata` field                 | Resolved URL                     |
457	| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
458	| `/`                              | `https://acme.com`               |
459	| `./`                             | `https://acme.com`               |
460	| `payments`                       | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
461	| `/payments`                      | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
462	| `./payments`                     | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
463	| `../payments`                    | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
464	| `https://beta.acme.com/payments` | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` |
465	
466	### `openGraph`
467	
468	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
469	export const metadata = {
470	  openGraph: {
471	    title: 'Next.js',
472	    description: 'The React Framework for the Web',
473	    url: 'https://nextjs.org',
474	    siteName: 'Next.js',
475	    images: [
476	      {
477	        url: 'https://nextjs.org/og.png', // Must be an absolute URL
478	        width: 800,
479	        height: 600,
480	      },
481	      {
482	        url: 'https://nextjs.org/og-alt.png', // Must be an absolute URL
483	        width: 1800,
484	        height: 1600,
485	        alt: 'My custom alt',
486	      },
487	    ],
488	    videos: [
489	      {
490	        url: 'https://nextjs.org/video.mp4', // Must be an absolute URL
491	        width: 800,
492	        height: 600,
493	      },
494	    ],
495	    audio: [
496	      {
497	        url: 'https://nextjs.org/audio.mp3', // Must be an absolute URL
498	      },
499	    ],
500	    locale: 'en_US',
501	    type: 'website',
502	  },
503	}
504	```
505	
506	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
507	<meta property="og:title" content="Next.js" />
508	<meta property="og:description" content="The React Framework for the Web" />
509	<meta property="og:url" content="https://nextjs.org/" />
510	<meta property="og:site_name" content="Next.js" />
511	<meta property="og:locale" content="en_US" />
512	<meta property="og:image" content="https://nextjs.org/og.png" />
513	<meta property="og:image:width" content="800" />
514	<meta property="og:image:height" content="600" />
515	<meta property="og:image" content="https://nextjs.org/og-alt.png" />
516	<meta property="og:image:width" content="1800" />
517	<meta property="og:image:height" content="1600" />
518	<meta property="og:image:alt" content="My custom alt" />
519	<meta property="og:video" content="https://nextjs.org/video.mp4" />
520	<meta property="og:video:width" content="800" />
521	<meta property="og:video:height" content="600" />
522	<meta property="og:audio" content="https://nextjs.org/audio.mp3" />
523	<meta property="og:type" content="website" />
524	```
525	
526	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
527	export const metadata = {
528	  openGraph: {
529	    title: 'Next.js',
530	    description: 'The React Framework for the Web',
531	    type: 'article',
532	    publishedTime: '2023-01-01T00:00:00.000Z',
533	    authors: ['Seb', 'Josh'],
534	  },
535	}

1048	### Types
1049	
1050	You can add type safety to your metadata by using the `Metadata` type. If you are using the [built-in TypeScript plugin](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript) in your IDE, you do not need to manually add the type, but you can still explicitly add it if you want.
1051	
1052	#### `metadata` object
1053	
1054	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1055	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1056	
1057	export const metadata: Metadata = {
1058	  title: 'Next.js',
1059	}
1060	```
1061	
1062	#### `generateMetadata` function
1063	
1064	##### Regular function
1065	
1066	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1067	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1068	
1069	export function generateMetadata(): Metadata {
1070	  return {
1071	    title: 'Next.js',
1072	  }
1073	}
1074	```
1075	
1076	##### Async function
1077	
1078	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1079	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1080	
1081	export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
1082	  return {
1083	    title: 'Next.js',
1084	  }
1085	}
1086	```
1087	
1088	##### With segment props
1089	
1090	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1091	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1092	
1093	type Props = {
1094	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
1095	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
1096	}
1097	
1098	export function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }: Props): Metadata {
1099	  return {
1100	    title: 'Next.js',
1101	  }
1102	}
1103	
1104	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
1105	```
1106	
1107	##### With parent metadata
1108	
1109	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1110	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
1111	
1112	export async function generateMetadata(
1113	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
1114	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
1115	): Promise<Metadata> {
1116	  return {
1117	    title: 'Next.js',
1118	  }
1119	}
1120	```

1123

1133	### Unsupported Metadata
1134	
1135	The following metadata types do not currently have built-in support. However, they can still be rendered in the layout or page itself.
1136	
1137	| Metadata                      | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
1138	| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1139	| `<meta http-equiv="...">`     | Use appropriate HTTP Headers via [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect), [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#nextresponse), [Security Headers](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers) |
1140	| `<base>`                      | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
1141	| `<noscript>`                  | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
1142	| `<style>`                     | Learn more about [styling in Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/css).                                                                                                                                                                        |
1143	| `<script>`                    | Learn more about [using scripts](/docs/app/guides/scripts).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
1144	| `<link rel="stylesheet" />`   | `import` stylesheets directly in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
1145	| `<link rel="preload" />`      | Use [ReactDOM preload method](#link-relpreload)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
1146	| `<link rel="preconnect" />`   | Use [ReactDOM preconnect method](#link-relpreconnect)                                                                                                                                                                                        |
1147	| `<link rel="dns-prefetch" />` | Use [ReactDOM prefetchDNS method](#link-reldns-prefetch)                                                                                                                                                                                     |

1149	### Resource hints
1150	
1151	The `<link>` element has a number of `rel` keywords that can be used to hint to the browser that an external resource is likely to be needed. The browser uses this information to apply preloading optimizations depending on the keyword.
1152	
1153	While the Metadata API doesn't directly support these hints, you can use new [`ReactDOM` methods](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/26237) to safely insert them into the `<head>` of the document.
1154	
1155	```tsx filename="app/preload-resources.tsx" switcher
1156	'use client'
1157	
1158	import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
1159	
1160	export function PreloadResources() {
1161	  ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
1162	  ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
1163	  ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
1164	
1165	  return '...'
1166	}
1167	```
1168	
1169	```jsx filename="app/preload-resources.js" switcher
1170	'use client'
1171	
1172	import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
1173	
1174	export function PreloadResources() {
1175	  ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
1176	  ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
1177	  ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
1178	
1179	  return '...'
1180	}
1181	```
1182	
1183	#### `<link rel="preload">`
1184	
1185	Start loading a resource early in the page rendering (browser) lifecycle. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload).
1186	
1187	```tsx
1188	ReactDOM.preload(href: string, options: { as: string })
1189	```
1190	
1191	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1192	<link rel="preload" href="..." as="..." />
1193	```
1194	
1195	##### `<link rel="preconnect">`
1196	
1197	Preemptively initiate a connection to an origin. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preconnect).
1198	
1199	```tsx
1200	ReactDOM.preconnect(href: string, options?: { crossOrigin?: string })
1201	```
1202	
1203	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1204	<link rel="preconnect" href="..." crossorigin />
1205	```
1206	
1207	#### `<link rel="dns-prefetch">`
1208	
1209	Attempt to resolve a domain name before resources get requested. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/dns-prefetch).
1210	
1211	```tsx
1212	ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(href: string)
1213	```
1214	
1215	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1216	<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="..." />
1217	```
1218	
1219	> **Good to know**:
1220	>
1221	> - These methods are currently only supported in Client Components, which are still Server Side Rendered on initial page load.
1222	> - Next.js in-built features such as `next/font`, `next/image` and `next/script` automatically handle relevant resource hints.
1223	
1224	## Behavior
1225	
1226	### Default Fields
1227	
1228	There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
1229	
1230	- The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
1231	- The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
1232	
1233	```html
1234	<meta charset="utf-8" />
1235	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
1236	```
1237	
1238	> **Good to know**: You can overwrite the default [`viewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.
1239	
1240	### Streaming metadata
1241	
1242	Streaming metadata allows Next.js to render and send the initial UI to the browser, without waiting for `generateMetadata` to complete.
1243	
1244	When `generateMetadata` resolves, the resulting metadata tags are appended to the `<body>` tag. We have verified that metadata is interpreted correctly by bots that execute JavaScript and inspect the full DOM (e.g. `Googlebot`).
1245	
1246	For **HTML-limited bots** that can’t execute JavaScript (e.g. `facebookexternalhit`), metadata continues to block page rendering. The resulting metadata will be available in the `<head>` tag.
1247	
1248	Next.js automatically detects **HTML-limited bots** by looking at the User Agent header. You can use the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) option in your Next.js config file to override the default [User Agent list](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/html-bots.ts).
1249	
1250	To fully disable streaming metadata:
1251	
1252	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
1253	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
1254	
1255	const config: NextConfig = {
1256	  htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
1257	}
1258	
1259	export default config
1260	```
1261	
1262	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
1263	module.exports = {
1264	  htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
1265	}
1266	```
1267	
1268	Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by reducing [TTFB](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) and can help lowering [LCP](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Largest_contentful_paint) time.
1269	
1270	Overriding `htmlLimitedBots` could lead to longer response times. Streaming metadata is an advanced feature, and the default should be sufficient for most cases.
1271	
1272	### With Cache Components
1273	
1274	When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `generateMetadata` follows the same rules as other components. If metadata accesses runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams`) or performs uncached data fetching, it defers to request time.
1275	
1276	How Next.js handles this depends on the rest of your page:
1277	
1278	- **If other parts also defer to request time**: Prerendering generates a static shell, and metadata streams in with other deferred content.
1279	- **If the page or layout is otherwise fully prerenderable**: Next.js requires an explicit choice: cache the data if possible, or signal that deferred rendering is intentional.
1280	
1281	Streaming metadata at runtime while the rest of the page is fully prerenderable is not common. To ensure this behavior is intentional, an error is raised indicating which page or layout needs to be handled.
1282	
1283	To resolve this, you have two options. If metadata depends on external data but not runtime data, use `use cache`:
1284	
1285	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={2}
1286	export async function generateMetadata() {
1287	  'use cache'
1288	  const { title, description } = await db.query('site-metadata')
1289	  return { title, description }
1290	}
1291	```
1292	
1293	If metadata genuinely requires runtime data, add a dynamic marker component to your page:
1294	
1295	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={11-14,19,31}
1296	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1297	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1298	import { connection } from 'next/server'
1299	
1300	export async function generateMetadata() {
1301	  const token = (await cookies()).get('token')?.value
1302	  // ... use token to fetch personalized metadata
1303	  return { title: 'Personalized Title' }
1304	}
1305	
1306	const Connection = async () => {
1307	  await connection()
1308	  return null
1309	}
1310	
1311	async function DynamicMarker() {
1312	  return (
1313	    <Suspense>
1314	      <Connection />
1315	    </Suspense>
1316	  )
1317	}
1318	
1319	export default function Page() {
1320	  // DO NOT place await connection() here
1321	  // doing so prevents the article tag content from
1322	  // being included in the static shell
1323	  return (
1324	    <>
1325	      <article>Static content</article>
1326	      <DynamicMarker />
1327	    </>
1328	  )
1329	}
1330	```
1331	
1332	The `DynamicMarker` component renders nothing but tells Next.js the page has intentional dynamic content. By wrapping it in Suspense, the static content still prerenders normally.
1333	
1334	See [Next.js encountered runtime data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) and [Next.js encountered uncached data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-dynamic) for full fix options and trade-offs.
1335	
1336	### Ordering
1337	
1338	Metadata is evaluated in order, starting from the root segment down to the segment closest to the final `page.js` segment. For example:
1339	
1340	1. `app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout)
1341	2. `app/blog/layout.tsx` (Nested Blog Layout)
1342	3. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (Blog Page)
1343	
1344	### Merging
1345	
1346	Following the [evaluation order](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are **shallowly** merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are **replaced** based on their ordering.
1347	
1348	This means metadata with nested fields such as [`openGraph`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are **overwritten** by the last segment to define them.
1349	
1350	#### Overwriting fields
1351	
1352	```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
1353	export const metadata = {
1354	  title: 'Acme',
1355	  openGraph: {
1356	    title: 'Acme',
1357	    description: 'Acme is a...',
1358	  },
1359	}
1360	```
1361	
1362	```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js"
1363	export const metadata = {
1364	  title: 'Blog',
1365	  openGraph: {
1366	    title: 'Blog',
1367	  },
1368	}
1369	
1370	// Output:
1371	// <title>Blog</title>
1372	// <meta property="og:title" content="Blog" />
1373	```
1374	
1375	In the example above:
1376	
1377	- `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/blog/page.js`.
1378	- All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **replaced** in `app/blog/page.js` because `app/blog/page.js` sets `openGraph` metadata. Note the absence of `openGraph.description`.
1379	
1380	If you'd like to share some nested fields between segments while overwriting others, you can pull them out into a separate variable:
1381	
1382	```jsx filename="app/shared-metadata.js"
1383	export const openGraphImage = { images: ['http://...'] }
1384	```
1385	
1386	```jsx filename="app/page.js"
1387	import { openGraphImage } from './shared-metadata'
1388	
1389	export const metadata = {
1390	  openGraph: {
1391	    ...openGraphImage,
1392	    title: 'Home',
1393	  },
1394	}
1395	```
1396	
1397	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
1398	import { openGraphImage } from '../shared-metadata'
1399	
1400	export const metadata = {
1401	  openGraph: {
1402	    ...openGraphImage,
1403	    title: 'About',
1404	  },
1405	}
1406	```
1407	
1408	In the example above, the OG image is shared between `app/layout.js` and `app/about/page.js` while the titles are different.
1409	
1410	#### Inheriting fields
1411	
1412	```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
1413	export const metadata = {
1414	  title: 'Acme',
1415	  openGraph: {
1416	    title: 'Acme',
1417	    description: 'Acme is a...',
1418	  },
1419	}
1420	```
1421	
1422	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
1423	export const metadata = {
1424	  title: 'About',
1425	}
1426	
1427	// Output:
1428	// <title>About</title>
1429	// <meta property="og:title" content="Acme" />
1430	// <meta property="og:description" content="Acme is a..." />
1431	```
1432	
1433	**Notes**
1434	
1435	- `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/about/page.js`.
1436	- All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **inherited** in `app/about/page.js` because `app/about/page.js` doesn't set `openGraph` metadata.
1437	
1438	## Version History
1439	
1440	| Version   | Changes                                                                                                                                                 |
1441	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1442	| `v15.2.0` | Introduced streaming support to `generateMetadata`.                                                                                                     |
1443	| `v14.0.0` | `viewport`, `themeColor`, and `colorScheme` deprecated in favor of the [`viewport` configuration](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport). |
1444	| `v13.2.0` | `metadata` and `generateMetadata` introduced.                                                                                                           |
1445

1	---
2	title: generateMetadata
3	description: Learn how to add Metadata to your Next.js application for improved search engine optimization (SEO) and web shareability.
4	related:
5	  title: Next Steps
6	  description: View all the Metadata API options.
7	  links:
8	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata
9	    - app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport
10	    - app/getting-started/caching
11	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
12	---
13	
14	You can use the `metadata` object or the `generateMetadata` function to define metadata.
15	
16	## The `metadata` object
17	
18	To define static metadata, export a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) from a `layout.js` or `page.js` file.
19	
20	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx" switcher
21	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
22	
23	export const metadata: Metadata = {
24	  title: '...',
25	  description: '...',
26	}
27	
28	export default function Page() {}
29	```
30	
31	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher
32	export const metadata = {
33	  title: '...',
34	  description: '...',
35	}
36	
37	export default function Page() {}
38	```
39	
40	> See the [Metadata Fields](#metadata-fields) for a complete list of supported options.
41	
42	## `generateMetadata` function
43	
44	Dynamic metadata depends on **dynamic information**, such as the current route parameters, external data, or `metadata` in parent segments, can be set by exporting a `generateMetadata` function that returns a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields).
45	
46	Resolving `generateMetadata` is part of rendering the page. If the page can be prerendered and `generateMetadata` doesn't introduce dynamic behavior, the resulting metadata is included in the page's initial HTML.
47	
48	Otherwise the metadata resolved from `generateMetadata` [can be streamed](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#streaming-metadata) after sending the initial UI.
49	
50	```tsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.tsx" switcher
51	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
52	
53	type Props = {
54	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
55	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
56	}
57	
58	export async function generateMetadata(
59	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
60	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
61	): Promise<Metadata> {
62	  // read route params
63	  const { id } = await params
64	
65	  // fetch data
66	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
67	
68	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
69	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
70	
71	  return {
72	    title: product.title,
73	    openGraph: {
74	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
75	    },
76	  }
77	}
78	
79	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
80	```
81	
82	```jsx filename="app/products/[id]/page.js" switcher
83	export async function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }, parent) {
84	  // read route params
85	  const { id } = await params
86	
87	  // fetch data
88	  const product = await fetch(`https://.../${id}`).then((res) => res.json())
89	
90	  // optionally access and extend (rather than replace) parent metadata
91	  const previousImages = (await parent).openGraph?.images || []
92	
93	  return {
94	    title: product.title,
95	    openGraph: {
96	      images: ['/some-specific-page-image.jpg', ...previousImages],
97	    },
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }) {}
102	```
103	
104	For type completion of `params` and `searchParams`, you can type the first argument with [`PageProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#page-props-helper) or [`LayoutProps<'/route'>`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout#layout-props-helper) for pages and layouts respectively.
105	
106	> **Good to know**:
107	>
108	> - Metadata can be added to `layout.js` and `page.js` files.
109	> - Next.js will automatically resolve the metadata, and create the relevant `<head>` tags for the page.
110	> - The `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function exports are **only supported in Server Components**.
111	> - You cannot export both the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function from the same route segment.
112	> - `fetch` requests inside `generateMetadata` are automatically [memoized](/docs/app/glossary#memoization) for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components.
113	> - React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
114	> - [File-based metadata](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata) has the higher priority and will override the `metadata` object and `generateMetadata` function.
115	
116	## Why `generateMetadata` is Server Component only
117	
118	`generateMetadata` and the `metadata` export are only supported in Server Components because metadata must be resolved on the server before the page component is rendered. This allows Next.js to include the metadata in the initial HTML response.
119	
120	If you need to use Client Component features, keep your `page.tsx` as a Server Component and move the Client Component logic to a separate file:
121	
122	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
123	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
124	import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
125	
126	export const metadata: Metadata = {
127	  title: 'My Page',
128	}
129	
130	export default function Page() {
131	  return <InteractiveComponent />
132	}
133	```
134	
135	```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
136	import { InteractiveComponent } from './interactive-component'
137	
138	export const metadata = {
139	  title: 'My Page',
140	}
141	
142	export default function Page() {
143	  return <InteractiveComponent />
144	}
145	```
146	
147	```tsx filename="app/interactive-component.tsx" switcher
148	'use client'
149	
150	export function InteractiveComponent() {
151	  // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
152	}
153	```
154	
155	```jsx filename="app/interactive-component.js" switcher
156	'use client'
157	
158	export function InteractiveComponent() {
159	  // Client-side interactivity (hooks, event handlers, etc.)
160	}
161	```
162	
163	## Reference
164	
165	### Parameters
166	
167	`generateMetadata` function accepts the following parameters:
168	
169	- `props` - An object containing the parameters of the current route:
170	  - `params` - An object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to the segment `generateMetadata` is called from. Examples:
171	
172	    | Route                           | URL         | `params`                  |
173	    | ------------------------------- | ----------- | ------------------------- |
174	    | `app/shop/[slug]/page.js`       | `/shop/1`   | `{ slug: '1' }`           |
175	    | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/page.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `{ tag: '1', item: '2' }` |
176	    | `app/shop/[...slug]/page.js`    | `/shop/1/2` | `{ slug: ['1', '2'] }`    |
177	
178	  - `searchParams` - An object containing the current URL's [search params](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Learn/Common_questions/What_is_a_URL#parameters). Examples:
179	
180	    | URL             | `searchParams`       |
181	    | --------------- | -------------------- |
182	    | `/shop?a=1`     | `{ a: '1' }`         |
183	    | `/shop?a=1&b=2` | `{ a: '1', b: '2' }` |
184	    | `/shop?a=1&a=2` | `{ a: ['1', '2'] }`  |
185	
186	- `parent` - A promise of the resolved metadata from parent route segments.
187	
188	### Returns
189	
190	`generateMetadata` should return a [`Metadata` object](#metadata-fields) containing one or more metadata fields.
191	
192	> **Good to know**:
193	>
194	> - If metadata doesn't depend on request information, it should be defined using the static [`metadata` object](#the-metadata-object) rather than `generateMetadata`.
195	> - `fetch` requests are automatically memoized for the same data across `generateMetadata`, `generateStaticParams`, Layouts, Pages, and Server Components. React [`cache` can be used](https://react.dev/reference/react/cache) if `fetch` is unavailable.
196	> - `searchParams` are only available in `page.js` segments.
197	> - The [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect) and [`notFound()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/not-found) Next.js methods can also be used inside `generateMetadata`.
198	
199	### Metadata Fields
200	
201	The following fields are supported:
202	
203	#### `title`
204	
205	The `title` attribute is used to set the title of the document. It can be defined as a simple [string](#string) or an optional [template object](#template).
206	
207	##### String
208	
209	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
210	export const metadata = {
211	  title: 'Next.js',
212	}
213	```
214	
215	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
216	<title>Next.js</title>
217	```
218	
219	##### `default`
220	
221	`title.default` can be used to provide a **fallback title** to child route segments that don't define a `title`.
222	
223	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx"
224	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
225	
226	export const metadata: Metadata = {
227	  title: {
228	    default: 'Acme',
229	  },
230	}
231	```
232	
233	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx"
234	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
235	
236	export const metadata: Metadata = {}
237	
238	// Output: <title>Acme</title>
239	```
240	
241	##### `template`
242	
243	`title.template` can be used to add a prefix or a suffix to `titles` defined in **child** route segments.
244	
245	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
246	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
247	
248	export const metadata: Metadata = {
249	  title: {
250	    template: '%s | Acme',
251	    default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
252	  },
253	}
254	```
255	
256	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
257	export const metadata = {
258	  title: {
259	    template: '%s | Acme',
260	    default: 'Acme', // a default is required when creating a template
261	  },
262	}
263	```
264	
265	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
266	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
267	
268	export const metadata: Metadata = {
269	  title: 'About',
270	}
271	
272	// Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
273	```
274	
275	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
276	export const metadata = {
277	  title: 'About',
278	}
279	
280	// Output: <title>About | Acme</title>
281	```
282	
283	> **Good to know**:
284	>
285	> - `title.template` applies to **child** route segments and **not** the segment it's defined in. This means:
286	>   - `title.default` is **required** when you add a `title.template`.
287	>   - `title.template` defined in `layout.js` will not apply to a `title` defined in a `page.js` of the same route segment.
288	>   - `title.template` defined in `page.js` has no effect because a page is always the terminating segment (it doesn't have any children route segments).
289	> - `title.template` has **no effect** if a route has not defined a `title` or `title.default`.
290	
291	##### `absolute`
292	
293	`title.absolute` can be used to provide a title that **ignores** `title.template` set in parent segments.
294	
295	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
296	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
297	
298	export const metadata: Metadata = {
299	  title: {
300	    template: '%s | Acme',
301	  },
302	}
303	```
304	
305	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
306	export const metadata = {
307	  title: {
308	    template: '%s | Acme',
309	  },
310	}
311	```
312	
313	```tsx filename="app/about/page.tsx" switcher
314	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
315	
316	export const metadata: Metadata = {
317	  title: {
318	    absolute: 'About',
319	  },
320	}
321	
322	// Output: <title>About</title>
323	```
324	
325	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js" switcher
326	export const metadata = {
327	  title: {
328	    absolute: 'About',
329	  },
330	}
331	
332	// Output: <title>About</title>
333	```
334	
335	> **Good to know**:
336	>
337	> - `layout.js`
338	>   - `title` (string) and `title.default` define the default title for child segments (that do not define their own `title`). It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
339	>   - `title.absolute` defines the default title for child segments. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
340	>   - `title.template` defines a new title template for child segments.
341	> - `page.js`
342	>   - If a page does not define its own title the closest parents resolved title will be used.
343	>   - `title` (string) defines the routes title. It will augment `title.template` from the closest parent segment if it exists.
344	>   - `title.absolute` defines the route title. It ignores `title.template` from parent segments.
345	>   - `title.template` has no effect in `page.js` because a page is always the terminating segment of a route.

391	#### `metadataBase`
392	
393	`metadataBase` is a convenience option to set a base URL prefix for `metadata` fields that require a fully qualified URL.
394	
395	- `metadataBase` allows URL-based `metadata` fields defined in the **current route segment and below** to use a **relative path** instead of an otherwise required absolute URL.
396	- The field's relative path will be composed with `metadataBase` to form a fully qualified URL.
397	
398	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
399	export const metadata = {
400	  metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
401	  alternates: {
402	    canonical: '/',
403	    languages: {
404	      'en-US': '/en-US',
405	      'de-DE': '/de-DE',
406	    },
407	  },
408	  openGraph: {
409	    images: '/og-image.png',
410	  },
411	}
412	```
413	
414	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
415	<link rel="canonical" href="https://acme.com" />
416	<link rel="alternate" hreflang="en-US" href="https://acme.com/en-US" />
417	<link rel="alternate" hreflang="de-DE" href="https://acme.com/de-DE" />
418	<meta property="og:image" content="https://acme.com/og-image.png" />
419	```
420	
421	> **Good to know**:
422	>
423	> - `metadataBase` is typically set in root `app/layout.js` to apply to URL-based `metadata` fields across all routes.
424	> - When `generateMetadata` uses `'use cache'`, its return value must be serializable. `URL` instances are not supported by Cache Functions, so values such as `metadataBase` should be returned as strings (for example, `url.toString()`). See [`use cache` serialization requirements](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#serialization).
425	> - All URL-based `metadata` fields that require absolute URLs can be configured with a `metadataBase` option.
426	> - `metadataBase` can contain a subdomain e.g. `https://app.acme.com` or base path e.g. `https://acme.com/start/from/here`
427	> - If a `metadata` field provides an absolute URL, `metadataBase` will be ignored.
428	> - Using a relative path in a URL-based `metadata` field without configuring a `metadataBase` will cause a build error.
429	> - Next.js will normalize duplicate slashes between `metadataBase` (e.g. `https://acme.com/`) and a relative field (e.g. `/path`) to a single slash (e.g. `https://acme.com/path`)
430	
431	#### URL Composition
432	
433	URL composition favors developer intent over default directory traversal semantics.
434	
435	- Trailing slashes between `metadataBase` and `metadata` fields are normalized.
436	- An "absolute" path in a `metadata` field (that typically would replace the whole URL path) is treated as a "relative" path (starting from the end of `metadataBase`).
437	
438	For example, given the following `metadataBase`:
439	
440	```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher
441	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
442	
443	export const metadata: Metadata = {
444	  metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
445	}
446	```
447	
448	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher
449	export const metadata = {
450	  metadataBase: new URL('https://acme.com'),
451	}
452	```
453	
454	Any `metadata` fields that inherit the above `metadataBase` and set their own value will be resolved as follows:
455	
456	| `metadata` field                 | Resolved URL                     |
457	| -------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
458	| `/`                              | `https://acme.com`               |
459	| `./`                             | `https://acme.com`               |
460	| `payments`                       | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
461	| `/payments`                      | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
462	| `./payments`                     | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
463	| `../payments`                    | `https://acme.com/payments`      |
464	| `https://beta.acme.com/payments` | `https://beta.acme.com/payments` |
