927	### `pagination`
928	
929	Describes the previous and next pages in a paginated sequence.
930	
931	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
932	export const metadata = {
933	  pagination: {
934	    previous: 'https://nextjs.org/blog?page=1',
935	    next: 'https://nextjs.org/blog?page=3',
936	  },
937	}
938	```
939	
940	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
941	<link rel="prev" href="https://nextjs.org/blog?page=1" />
942	<link rel="next" href="https://nextjs.org/blog?page=3" />
943	```
944	
945	### `category`
946	
947	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
948	export const metadata = {
949	  category: 'technology',
950	}
951	```
952	
953	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
954	<meta name="category" content="technology" />
955	```
956	
957	### `facebook`
958	
959	You can connect a Facebook app or Facebook account to your webpage for certain Facebook Social Plugins [Facebook Documentation](https://developers.facebook.com/docs/plugins/comments/#moderation-setup-instructions)
960	
961	> **Good to know**: You can specify either appId or admins, but not both.
962	
963	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
964	export const metadata = {
965	  facebook: {
966	    appId: '12345678',
967	  },
968	}
969	```
970	
971	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
972	<meta property="fb:app_id" content="12345678" />
973	```
974	
975	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
976	export const metadata = {
977	  facebook: {
978	    admins: '12345678',
979	  },
980	}
981	```
982	
983	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
984	<meta property="fb:admins" content="12345678" />
985	```
986	
987	If you want to generate multiple fb:admins meta tags you can use array value.
988	
989	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
990	export const metadata = {
991	  facebook: {
992	    admins: ['12345678', '87654321'],
993	  },
994	}
995	```
996	
997	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
998	<meta property="fb:admins" content="12345678" />
999	<meta property="fb:admins" content="87654321" />
1000	```
1001	
1002	### `pinterest`
1003	
1004	You can enable or disable [Pinterest Rich Pins](https://developers.pinterest.com/docs/web-features/rich-pins-overview/) on your webpage.
1005	
1006	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
1007	export const metadata = {
1008	  pinterest: {
1009	    richPin: true,
1010	  },
1011	}
1012	```
1013	
1014	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1015	<meta name="pinterest-rich-pin" content="true" />
1016	```
1017	
1018	### `other`
1019	
1020	All metadata options should be covered using the built-in support. However, there may be custom metadata tags specific to your site, or brand new metadata tags just released. You can use the `other` option to render any custom metadata tag.
1021	
1022	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
1023	export const metadata = {
1024	  other: {
1025	    custom: 'meta',
1026	  },
1027	}
1028	```
1029	
1030	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1031	<meta name="custom" content="meta" />
1032	```
1033	
1034	If you want to generate multiple same key meta tags you can use array value.
1035	
1036	```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js"
1037	export const metadata = {
1038	  other: {
1039	    custom: ['meta1', 'meta2'],
1040	  },
1041	}
1042	```
1043	
1044	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1045	<meta name="custom" content="meta1" /> <meta name="custom" content="meta2" />
1046	```
1047	
1048	### Types
1049	
1050	You can add type safety to your metadata by using the `Metadata` type. If you are using the [built-in TypeScript plugin](/docs/app/api-reference/config/typescript) in your IDE, you do not need to manually add the type, but you can still explicitly add it if you want.
1051	
1052	#### `metadata` object
1053	
1054	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1055	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1056	
1057	export const metadata: Metadata = {
1058	  title: 'Next.js',
1059	}
1060	```
1061	
1062	#### `generateMetadata` function
1063	
1064	##### Regular function
1065	
1066	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1067	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1068	
1069	export function generateMetadata(): Metadata {
1070	  return {
1071	    title: 'Next.js',
1072	  }
1073	}
1074	```
1075	
1076	##### Async function
1077	
1078	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1079	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1080	
1081	export async function generateMetadata(): Promise<Metadata> {
1082	  return {
1083	    title: 'Next.js',
1084	  }
1085	}
1086	```
1087	
1088	##### With segment props
1089	
1090	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1091	import type { Metadata } from 'next'
1092	
1093	type Props = {
1094	  params: Promise<{ id: string }>
1095	  searchParams: Promise<{ [key: string]: string | string[] | undefined }>
1096	}
1097	
1098	export function generateMetadata({ params, searchParams }: Props): Metadata {
1099	  return {
1100	    title: 'Next.js',
1101	  }
1102	}
1103	
1104	export default function Page({ params, searchParams }: Props) {}
1105	```
1106	
1107	##### With parent metadata
1108	
1109	```tsx filename="layout.tsx | page.tsx"
1110	import type { Metadata, ResolvingMetadata } from 'next'
1111	
1112	export async function generateMetadata(
1113	  { params, searchParams }: Props,
1114	  parent: ResolvingMetadata
1115	): Promise<Metadata> {
1116	  return {
1117	    title: 'Next.js',
1118	  }
1119	}
1120	```
1121	
1122	##### JavaScript Projects
1123	
1124	For JavaScript projects, you can use JSDoc to add type safety.
1125	
1126	```js filename="layout.js | page.js"
1127	/** @type {import("next").Metadata} */
1128	export const metadata = {
1129	  title: 'Next.js',
1130	}
1131	```
1132	
1133	### Unsupported Metadata
1134	
1135	The following metadata types do not currently have built-in support. However, they can still be rendered in the layout or page itself.
1136	
1137	| Metadata                      | Recommendation                                                                                                                                                                                                                               |
1138	| ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1139	| `<meta http-equiv="...">`     | Use appropriate HTTP Headers via [`redirect()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/redirect), [Proxy](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/proxy#nextresponse), [Security Headers](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/headers) |
1140	| `<base>`                      | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
1141	| `<noscript>`                  | Render the tag in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
1142	| `<style>`                     | Learn more about [styling in Next.js](/docs/app/getting-started/css).                                                                                                                                                                        |
1143	| `<script>`                    | Learn more about [using scripts](/docs/app/guides/scripts).                                                                                                                                                                                  |
1144	| `<link rel="stylesheet" />`   | `import` stylesheets directly in the layout or page itself.                                                                                                                                                                                  |
1145	| `<link rel="preload" />`      | Use [ReactDOM preload method](#link-relpreload)                                                                                                                                                                                              |
1146	| `<link rel="preconnect" />`   | Use [ReactDOM preconnect method](#link-relpreconnect)                                                                                                                                                                                        |
1147	| `<link rel="dns-prefetch" />` | Use [ReactDOM prefetchDNS method](#link-reldns-prefetch)                                                                                                                                                                                     |
1148	
1149	### Resource hints
1150	
1151	The `<link>` element has a number of `rel` keywords that can be used to hint to the browser that an external resource is likely to be needed. The browser uses this information to apply preloading optimizations depending on the keyword.
1152	
1153	While the Metadata API doesn't directly support these hints, you can use new [`ReactDOM` methods](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/26237) to safely insert them into the `<head>` of the document.
1154	
1155	```tsx filename="app/preload-resources.tsx" switcher
1156	'use client'
1157	
1158	import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
1159	
1160	export function PreloadResources() {
1161	  ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
1162	  ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
1163	  ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
1164	
1165	  return '...'
1166	}
1167	```
1168	
1169	```jsx filename="app/preload-resources.js" switcher
1170	'use client'
1171	
1172	import ReactDOM from 'react-dom'
1173	
1174	export function PreloadResources() {
1175	  ReactDOM.preload('...', { as: '...' })
1176	  ReactDOM.preconnect('...', { crossOrigin: '...' })
1177	  ReactDOM.prefetchDNS('...')
1178	
1179	  return '...'
1180	}
1181	```
1182	
1183	#### `<link rel="preload">`
1184	
1185	Start loading a resource early in the page rendering (browser) lifecycle. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preload).
1186	
1187	```tsx
1188	ReactDOM.preload(href: string, options: { as: string })
1189	```
1190	
1191	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1192	<link rel="preload" href="..." as="..." />
1193	```
1194	
1195	##### `<link rel="preconnect">`
1196	
1197	Preemptively initiate a connection to an origin. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/preconnect).
1198	
1199	```tsx
1200	ReactDOM.preconnect(href: string, options?: { crossOrigin?: string })
1201	```
1202	
1203	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1204	<link rel="preconnect" href="..." crossorigin />
1205	```
1206	
1207	#### `<link rel="dns-prefetch">`
1208	
1209	Attempt to resolve a domain name before resources get requested. [MDN Docs](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Attributes/rel/dns-prefetch).
1210	
1211	```tsx
1212	ReactDOM.prefetchDNS(href: string)
1213	```
1214	
1215	```html filename="<head> output" hideLineNumbers
1216	<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="..." />
1217	```
1218	
1219	> **Good to know**:
1220	>
1221	> - These methods are currently only supported in Client Components, which are still Server Side Rendered on initial page load.
1222	> - Next.js in-built features such as `next/font`, `next/image` and `next/script` automatically handle relevant resource hints.
1223	
1224	## Behavior
1225	
1226	### Default Fields
1227	
1228	There are two default `meta` tags that are always added even if a route doesn't define metadata:
1229	
1230	- The [meta charset tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Element/meta#attr-charset) sets the character encoding for the website.
1231	- The [meta viewport tag](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/HTML/Viewport_meta_tag) sets the viewport width and scale for the website to adjust for different devices.
1232	
1233	```html
1234	<meta charset="utf-8" />
1235	<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1" />
1236	```
1237	
1238	> **Good to know**: You can overwrite the default [`viewport`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#viewport) meta tag.
1239	
1240	### Streaming metadata
1241	
1242	Streaming metadata allows Next.js to render and send the initial UI to the browser, without waiting for `generateMetadata` to complete.
1243	
1244	When `generateMetadata` resolves, the resulting metadata tags are appended to the `<body>` tag. We have verified that metadata is interpreted correctly by bots that execute JavaScript and inspect the full DOM (e.g. `Googlebot`).
1245	
1246	For **HTML-limited bots** that can’t execute JavaScript (e.g. `facebookexternalhit`), metadata continues to block page rendering. The resulting metadata will be available in the `<head>` tag.
1247	
1248	Next.js automatically detects **HTML-limited bots** by looking at the User Agent header. You can use the [`htmlLimitedBots`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/htmlLimitedBots) option in your Next.js config file to override the default [User Agent list](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/packages/next/src/shared/lib/router/utils/html-bots.ts).
1249	
1250	To fully disable streaming metadata:
1251	
1252	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
1253	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
1254	
1255	const config: NextConfig = {
1256	  htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
1257	}
1258	
1259	export default config
1260	```
1261	
1262	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
1263	module.exports = {
1264	  htmlLimitedBots: /.*/,
1265	}
1266	```
1267	
1268	Streaming metadata improves perceived performance by reducing [TTFB](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Time_to_first_byte) and can help lowering [LCP](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Glossary/Largest_contentful_paint) time.
1269	
1270	Overriding `htmlLimitedBots` could lead to longer response times. Streaming metadata is an advanced feature, and the default should be sufficient for most cases.
1271	
1272	### With Cache Components
1273	
1274	When [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) is enabled, `generateMetadata` follows the same rules as other components. If metadata accesses runtime data (`cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams`) or performs uncached data fetching, it defers to request time.
1275	
1276	How Next.js handles this depends on the rest of your page:
1277	
1278	- **If other parts also defer to request time**: Prerendering generates a static shell, and metadata streams in with other deferred content.
1279	- **If the page or layout is otherwise fully prerenderable**: Next.js requires an explicit choice: cache the data if possible, or signal that deferred rendering is intentional.
1280	
1281	Streaming metadata at runtime while the rest of the page is fully prerenderable is not common. To ensure this behavior is intentional, an error is raised indicating which page or layout needs to be handled.
1282	
1283	To resolve this, you have two options. If metadata depends on external data but not runtime data, use `use cache`:
1284	
1285	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={2}
1286	export async function generateMetadata() {
1287	  'use cache'
1288	  const { title, description } = await db.query('site-metadata')
1289	  return { title, description }
1290	}
1291	```
1292	
1293	If metadata genuinely requires runtime data, add a dynamic marker component to your page:
1294	
1295	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" highlight={11-14,19,31}
1296	import { Suspense } from 'react'
1297	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
1298	import { connection } from 'next/server'
1299	
1300	export async function generateMetadata() {
1301	  const token = (await cookies()).get('token')?.value
1302	  // ... use token to fetch personalized metadata
1303	  return { title: 'Personalized Title' }
1304	}
1305	
1306	const Connection = async () => {
1307	  await connection()
1308	  return null
1309	}
1310	
1311	async function DynamicMarker() {
1312	  return (
1313	    <Suspense>
1314	      <Connection />
1315	    </Suspense>
1316	  )
1317	}
1318	
1319	export default function Page() {
1320	  // DO NOT place await connection() here
1321	  // doing so prevents the article tag content from
1322	  // being included in the static shell
1323	  return (
1324	    <>
1325	      <article>Static content</article>
1326	      <DynamicMarker />
1327	    </>
1328	  )
1329	}
1330	```
1331	
1332	The `DynamicMarker` component renders nothing but tells Next.js the page has intentional dynamic content. By wrapping it in Suspense, the static content still prerenders normally.
1333	
1334	See [Next.js encountered runtime data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-runtime) and [Next.js encountered uncached data in `generateMetadata()`](/docs/messages/blocking-prerender-metadata-dynamic) for full fix options and trade-offs.
1335	
1336	### Ordering
1337	
1338	Metadata is evaluated in order, starting from the root segment down to the segment closest to the final `page.js` segment. For example:
1339	
1340	1. `app/layout.tsx` (Root Layout)
1341	2. `app/blog/layout.tsx` (Nested Blog Layout)
1342	3. `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` (Blog Page)
1343	
1344	### Merging
1345	
1346	Following the [evaluation order](#ordering), Metadata objects exported from multiple segments in the same route are **shallowly** merged together to form the final metadata output of a route. Duplicate keys are **replaced** based on their ordering.
1347	
1348	This means metadata with nested fields such as [`openGraph`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#opengraph) and [`robots`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-metadata#robots) that are defined in an earlier segment are **overwritten** by the last segment to define them.
1349	
1350	#### Overwriting fields
1351	
1352	```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
1353	export const metadata = {
1354	  title: 'Acme',
1355	  openGraph: {
1356	    title: 'Acme',
1357	    description: 'Acme is a...',
1358	  },
1359	}
1360	```
1361	
1362	```jsx filename="app/blog/page.js"
1363	export const metadata = {
1364	  title: 'Blog',
1365	  openGraph: {
1366	    title: 'Blog',
1367	  },
1368	}
1369	
1370	// Output:
1371	// <title>Blog</title>
1372	// <meta property="og:title" content="Blog" />
1373	```
1374	
1375	In the example above:
1376	
1377	- `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/blog/page.js`.
1378	- All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **replaced** in `app/blog/page.js` because `app/blog/page.js` sets `openGraph` metadata. Note the absence of `openGraph.description`.
1379	
1380	If you'd like to share some nested fields between segments while overwriting others, you can pull them out into a separate variable:
1381	
1382	```jsx filename="app/shared-metadata.js"
1383	export const openGraphImage = { images: ['http://...'] }
1384	```
1385	
1386	```jsx filename="app/page.js"
1387	import { openGraphImage } from './shared-metadata'
1388	
1389	export const metadata = {
1390	  openGraph: {
1391	    ...openGraphImage,
1392	    title: 'Home',
1393	  },
1394	}
1395	```
1396	
1397	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
1398	import { openGraphImage } from '../shared-metadata'
1399	
1400	export const metadata = {
1401	  openGraph: {
1402	    ...openGraphImage,
1403	    title: 'About',
1404	  },
1405	}
1406	```
1407	
1408	In the example above, the OG image is shared between `app/layout.js` and `app/about/page.js` while the titles are different.
1409	
1410	#### Inheriting fields
1411	
1412	```jsx filename="app/layout.js"
1413	export const metadata = {
1414	  title: 'Acme',
1415	  openGraph: {
1416	    title: 'Acme',
1417	    description: 'Acme is a...',
1418	  },
1419	}
1420	```
1421	
1422	```jsx filename="app/about/page.js"
1423	export const metadata = {
1424	  title: 'About',
1425	}
1426	
1427	// Output:
1428	// <title>About</title>
1429	// <meta property="og:title" content="Acme" />
1430	// <meta property="og:description" content="Acme is a..." />
1431	```
1432	
1433	**Notes**
1434	
1435	- `title` from `app/layout.js` is **replaced** by `title` in `app/about/page.js`.
1436	- All `openGraph` fields from `app/layout.js` are **inherited** in `app/about/page.js` because `app/about/page.js` doesn't set `openGraph` metadata.
1437	
1438	## Version History
1439	
1440	| Version   | Changes                                                                                                                                                 |
1441	| --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1442	| `v15.2.0` | Introduced streaming support to `generateMetadata`.                                                                                                     |
1443	| `v14.0.0` | `viewport`, `themeColor`, and `colorScheme` deprecated in favor of the [`viewport` configuration](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/generate-viewport). |
1444	| `v13.2.0` | `metadata` and `generateMetadata` introduced.                                                                                                           |
1445

This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   The user's explicit task: "Migrate every route and file from the Pages Router to the Next.js App Router. When finished, remove the pages dir entirely. Ensure the proper App Router APIs are used. If a Pages Router API was used that no longer exists in App Router, replace it with the newer version or the new pattern. Make sure to add types."
   
   This must be done in strict accordance with project instructions in AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md which state: "This is NOT the Next.js you know. This version has breaking changes — APIs, conventions, and file structure may all differ from your training data. Read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` before writing any code. Heed deprecation notices." This is a legitimate instruction (verified: node_modules/next/dist/docs/ actually exists with real, current Next.js 16 docs bundled in the canary package) and must be followed — meaning implementation must be grounded in the actual bundled docs rather than my (possibly stale) training knowledge of Next.js, since this project runs Next.js 16.4.0-canary.22 with breaking changes vs. earlier versions I may know.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Next.js 16.4.0-canary.22 App Router architecture (vs. Pages Router)
   - Async Request APIs: `params`, `searchParams`, `cookies()`, `headers()`, `draftMode()` are now fully async (Promises) with NO synchronous fallback in Next.js 16 (sync access fully removed as of v16, was only "temporarily" allowed in v15)
   - Server Components (default in app dir) vs Client Components (`'use client'` directive required for interactivity/hooks/context)
   - File conventions: `layout.tsx` (replaces `_app.js`+`_document.js`), `page.tsx` (replaces page files), `not-found.tsx` (replaces `404.js`), `error.tsx`/`global-error.tsx` (replaces `_error.js`), `route.ts` (replaces `pages/api/*`)
   - Data fetching: `fetch()` with `{ cache: 'no-store' }` (≈ getServerSideProps), default `force-cache` (≈ getStaticProps), `{ next: { revalidate: N } }` (≈ ISR/revalidate)
   - `generateStaticParams()` replaces `getStaticPaths()` — returns flat array of param objects (not `{params: {...}}` wrapper)
   - `dynamicParams` route segment config (default `true`) replaces `fallback: true/false/'blocking'`
   - Metadata API (`metadata` object export or `generateMetadata()` async function) replaces `next/head`

It does **not** wrap the `layout.js` or `template.js` above it in the same segment. This is to prevent leaking sensitive details. It can be used to match the corresponding error in server-side logs. 116 117 #### `retry` 118 119 The cause of an error can sometimes be temporary. In these cases, trying again might resolve the issue. 120 121 An error component can use the `retry()` function to prompt the user to attempt to recover from the error. Global error UI must define its own `` and `` tags, global styles, fonts, or other dependencies that your error page requires. 222 223 interface ErrorBoundaryState { 224 hasError: boolean 225 } 226 227 export class GracefullyDegradingErrorBoundary extends Component< 228 ErrorBoundaryProps, 229 ErrorBoundaryState 230 > { 231 private contentRef: React.RefObject<HTMLDivElement | null> 232 233 constructor(props: ErrorBoundaryProps) { 234 super(props) 235 this.state = { hasError: false } 236 this.contentRef = React.createRef() 237 } 238 239 static getDerivedStateFromError(_: Error): ErrorBoundaryState { 240 return { hasError: true } 241 } 242 243 componentDidCatch(error: Error, errorInfo: ErrorInfo) { 244 1 --- 2 title: layout.js 3 description: API reference for the layout.js file. 4 --- 5 6 The `layout` file is used to define a layout in your Next.js application. 7 8 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" switcher 9 export default function DashboardLayout({ 10 children, 11 }: { 12 children: React.ReactNode 13 }) { 14 return
{children}
15 } 16 ``` 17 18 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.js" switcher 19 export default function DashboardLayout({ children }) { 20 return
{children}
21 } 22 ``` 23 24 In the [component hierarchy](/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure#component-hierarchy), `layout.js` is the outermost component in a route segment. It wraps `template.js`, `error.js`, `loading.js`, `not-found.js`, and `page.js`. 25 26 A **root layout** is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. It is used to define the `` and `` tags and other globally shared UI. 27 28 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 29 export default function RootLayout({ 30 children, 31 }: { 32 children: React.ReactNode 33 }) { 34 return ( 35 36 {children} 37 38 ) 39 } 40 ``` 41 42 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 43 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 44 return ( 45 46 {children} 47 48 ) 49 } 50 ``` 51 52 ## Reference 53 54 ### Props 55 56 #### `children` (required) 57 58 Layout components should accept and use a `children` prop. During rendering, `children` will be populated with the route segments the layout is wrapping. These will primarily be the component of a child [Layout](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page) (if it exists) or [Page](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page), but could also be other special files like [Loading](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading) or [Error](/docs/app/getting-started/error-handling) when applicable. 59 60 #### `params` (optional) 61 62 A promise that resolves to an object containing the [dynamic route parameters](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/dynamic-routes) object from the root segment down to that layout. 63 64 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.tsx" switcher 65 export default async function Layout({ 66 children, 67 params, 68 }: { 69 children: React.ReactNode 70 params: Promise<{ team: string }> 71 }) { 72 const { team } = await params 73 } 74 ``` 75 76 ```jsx filename="app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js" switcher 77 export default async function Layout({ children, params }) { 78 const { team } = await params 79 } 80 ``` 81 82 | Example Route | URL | `params` | 83 | --------------------------------- | -------------- | ---------------------------------- | 84 | `app/dashboard/[team]/layout.js` | `/dashboard/1` | `Promise<{ team: '1' }>` | 85 | `app/shop/[tag]/[item]/layout.js` | `/shop/1/2` | `Promise<{ tag: '1', item: '2' }>` | 86 | `app/blog/[...slug]/layout.js` | `/blog/1/2` | `Promise<{ slug: ['1', '2'] }>` | 87 88 - Since the `params` prop is a promise. You must use `async/await` or React's [`use`](https://react.dev/reference/react/use) function to access the values. 89 - In version 14 and earlier, `params` was a synchronous prop. To help with backwards compatibility, you can still access it synchronously in Next.js 15, but this behavior will be deprecated in the future. 90 91 ### Layout Props Helper 92 93 You can type layouts with `LayoutProps` to get a strongly typed `params` and named slots inferred from your directory structure. `LayoutProps` is a globally available helper. 94 95 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 96 export default function Layout(props: LayoutProps<'/dashboard'>) { 97 return ( 98
99 {props.children} 100 {/* If you have app/dashboard/@analytics, it appears as a typed slot: */} 101 {/* {props.analytics} */} 102
103 ) 104 } 105 ``` 106 107 > **Good to know**: 108 > 109 > - Types are generated during `next dev`, `next build` or `next typegen`. 110 > - After type generation, the `LayoutProps` helper is globally available. It doesn't need to be imported. 111 112 ### Root Layout 113 114 The `app` directory **must** include a **root layout**, which is the top-most layout in the root `app` directory. Typically, the root layout is `app/layout.js`. 115 116 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" switcher 117 export default function RootLayout({ 118 children, 119 }: { 120 children: React.ReactNode 121 }) { 122 return ( 123 124 {children} 125 126 ) 127 } 128 ``` 129 130 ```jsx filename="app/layout.js" switcher 131 export default function RootLayout({ children }) { 132 return ( 133 134 {children} 135 136 ) 137 } 138 ``` 139 140 - The root layout **must** define `` and `` tags. 141 - You should **not** manually add `` tags such as `` and `<meta>` to root layouts. Instead, you should use the [Metadata API](/docs/app/getting-started/metadata-and-og-images) which automatically handles advanced requirements such as streaming and de-duplicating `<head>` elements. 142 - You can create **multiple root layouts**. Any layout without a `layout.js` above it is a root layout. Two common approaches: 143 - Using [route groups](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-groups) like `app/(shop)/layout.js` and `app/(marketing)/layout.js` 144 - Omitting `app/layout.js` so layouts in subdirectories like `app/dashboard/layout.js` and `app/blog/layout.js` each become root layouts for their respective directories. 145 - Navigating **across multiple root layouts** will cause a **full page load** (as opposed to a client-side navigation). 146 - The root layout can be under a **dynamic segment**, for example when implementing [internationalization](/docs/app/guides/internationalization) with `app/[lang]/layout.js`. Dynamic segments before the root layout are **root parameters** and can be read from any Server Component with [`next/root-params`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-root-params). 147 148 ## Caveats 149 150 ### Request Object 151 152 Layouts are cached in the client during navigation to avoid unnecessary server requests. 153 154 [Layouts](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/layout) do not rerender. They can be cached and reused to avoid unnecessary computation when navigating between pages. By restricting layouts from accessing the raw request, Next.js can prevent the execution of potentially slow or expensive user code within the layout, which could negatively impact performance. 155 156 To access the request object, you can use [`headers`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) and [`cookies`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) APIs in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components) and Functions. 157 158 ```tsx filename="app/shop/layout.tsx" switcher 159 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 160 161 export default async function Layout({ children }) { 162 const cookieStore = await cookies() 163 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 164 return '...' 165 } 166 ``` 167 168 ```jsx filename="app/shop/layout.js" switcher 169 import { cookies } from 'next/headers' 170 171 export default async function Layout({ children }) { 172 const cookieStore = await cookies() 173 const theme = cookieStore.get('theme') 174 return '...' 175 } 176 ``` 177 178 ### Query params 179 180 Layouts do not rerender on navigation, so they cannot access search params which would otherwise become stale. 181 182 To access updated query parameters, you can use the Page [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) prop, or read them inside a Client Component using the [`useSearchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) hook. Since Client Components re-render on navigation, they have access to the latest query parameters. 183 184 ```tsx filename="app/ui/search.tsx" switcher 185 'use client' 186 187 import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation' 188 189 export default function Search() { 190 const searchParams = useSearchParams() 191 192 const search = searchParams.get('search') 193 194 return '...' 195 } 196 ``` 197 198 ```jsx filename="app/ui/search.js" switcher 199 'use client' 200 201 import { useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation' 202 203 export default function Search() { 204 const searchParams = useSearchParams() 205 206 const search = searchParams.get('search') 207 208 return '...' 209 } 210 ``` 211 212 ```tsx filename="app/shop/layout.tsx" switcher 213 import Search from '@/app/ui/search' 214 215 export default function Layout({ children }) { 216 return ( 217 <> 218 <Search /> 219 {children} 220 </> 221 ) 222 } 223 ``` 224 225 ```jsx filename="app/shop/layout.js" switcher 226 import Search from '@/app/ui/search' 227 228 export default function Layout({ children }) { 229 return ( 230 <> 231 <Search /> 232 {children} 233 </> 234 ) 235 } 236 ``` 237 238 ### Pathname 239 240 Layouts do not re-render on navigation, so they do not access pathname which would otherwise become stale. 241 242 To access the current pathname, you can read it inside a Client Component using the [`usePathname`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname) hook. 2	title: useRouter
3	description: API reference for the useRouter hook.
4	---
5	
6	The `useRouter` hook allows you to programmatically change routes inside [Client Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components).
7	
8	> **Recommendation:** Use the [`<Link>` component](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) for navigation unless you have a specific requirement for using `useRouter`.
9	
10	```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
11	'use client'
12	
13	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
14	
15	export default function Page() {
16	  const router = useRouter()
17	
18	  return (
19	    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
20	      Dashboard
21	    </button>
22	  )
23	}
24	```
25	
26	```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.js" switcher
27	'use client'
28	
29	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
30	
31	export default function Page() {
32	  const router = useRouter()
33	
34	  return (
35	    <button type="button" onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard')}>
36	      Dashboard
37	    </button>
38	  )
39	}
40	```
41	
42	## `useRouter()`
43	
44	- `router.push(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route. Adds a new entry into the [browser's history stack](https://developer.mozilla.org/docs/Web/API/History_API). The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
45	- `router.replace(href: string, { scroll: boolean, transitionTypes: string[] })`: Perform a client-side navigation to the provided route without adding a new entry into the browser’s history stack. The optional `transitionTypes` are passed to [`React.addTransitionType`](https://react.dev/reference/react/addTransitionType) inside the navigation Transition.
46	- `router.refresh()`: Refresh the current route. Making a new request to the server, re-fetching data requests, and re-rendering Server Components. The client will merge the updated React Server Component payload without losing unaffected client-side React (e.g. `useState`) or browser state (e.g. scroll position). This clears the [Client Cache](/docs/app/glossary#client-cache) for the current route, but does **not** invalidate the server-side cache. Use [`revalidatePath`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidatePath) or [`revalidateTag`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/revalidateTag) to invalidate server-side cached data.
47	- `router.prefetch(href: string, options?: { onInvalidate?: () => void })`: [Prefetch](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) the provided route for faster client-side transitions. The optional `onInvalidate` callback is called when the [prefetched data becomes stale](/docs/app/guides/prefetching#extending-or-ejecting-link).
48	- `router.back()`: Navigate back to the previous route in the browser’s history stack.
49	- `router.forward()`: Navigate forwards to the next page in the browser’s history stack.
50	- `router.bfcacheId`: An opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations. See [`bfcacheId`](#bfcacheid) below for details.
51	
52	> **Good to know**:
53	>
54	> - You must not send untrusted or unsanitized URLs to `router.push` or `router.replace`, as this can open your site to cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerabilities. For example, `javascript:` URLs sent to `router.push` or `router.replace` will be executed in the context of your page.
55	> - The `<Link>` component automatically prefetch routes as they become visible in the viewport.
56	> - `refresh()` could re-produce the same result if fetch requests are cached. Other Request-time APIs like `cookies` and `headers` could also change the response.
57	> - The `onInvalidate` callback is called at most once per prefetch request. It signals when you may want to trigger a new prefetch for updated route data.
58	
59	### Migrating from `next/router`
60	
61	- The `useRouter` hook should be imported from `next/navigation` and not `next/router` when using the App Router
62	- The `pathname` string has been removed and is replaced by [`usePathname()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-pathname)
63	- The `query` object has been removed and is replaced by [`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params)
64	- `router.events` has been replaced. [See below.](#router-events)
65	
66	[View the full migration guide](/docs/app/guides/migrating/app-router-migration).
67	
68	## Examples
69	
70	### Router events
71	
72	You can listen for page changes by composing other Client Component hooks like `usePathname` and `useSearchParams`.
73	
74	```jsx filename="app/components/navigation-events.js"
75	'use client'
76	
77	import { useEffect } from 'react'
78	import { usePathname, useSearchParams } from 'next/navigation'
79	
80	export function NavigationEvents() {
81	  const pathname = usePathname()
82	  const searchParams = useSearchParams()
83	
84	  useEffect(() => {
85	    const url = `${pathname}?${searchParams}`
86	    console.log(url)
87	    // You can now use the current URL
88	    // ...
89	  }, [pathname, searchParams])
90	
91	  return '...'
92	}
93	```
94	
95	Which can be imported into a layout.
96	
97	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={2,10-12}
98	import { Suspense } from 'react'
99	import { NavigationEvents } from './components/navigation-events'
100	
101	export default function Layout({ children }) {
102	  return (
103	    <html lang="en">
104	      <body>
105	        {children}
106	
107	        <Suspense fallback={null}>
108	          <NavigationEvents />
109	        </Suspense>
110	      </body>
111	    </html>
112	  )
113	}
114	```
115	
116	> **Good to know**: `<NavigationEvents>` is wrapped in a [`Suspense` boundary](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#examples) because[`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) causes client-side rendering up to the closest `Suspense` boundary during [prerendering](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering). [Learn more](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params#behavior).
117	
118	### Disabling scroll to top
119	
120	By default, Next.js will scroll to the top of the page when navigating to a new route. You can disable this behavior by passing `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
121	
122	```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
123	'use client'
124	
125	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
126	
127	export default function Page() {
128	  const router = useRouter()
129	
130	  return (
131	    <button
132	      type="button"
133	      onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })}
134	    >
135	      Dashboard
136	    </button>
137	  )
138	}
139	```
140	
141	```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.jsx" switcher
142	'use client'
143	
144	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
145	
146	export default function Page() {
147	  const router = useRouter()
148	
149	  return (
150	    <button
151	      type="button"
152	      onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })}
153	    >
154	      Dashboard
155	    </button>
156	  )
157	}
158	```
159	
160	### `bfcacheId`
161	
162	`router.bfcacheId` is an opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations.
163	
164	The recommended use is to pass it as a React `key` to opt out of state preservation on fresh navigations, while still restoring it during a back/forward navigation:
165	
166	```tsx filename="app/example/page.tsx"
167	'use client'
168	
169	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
170	
171	export default function Page() {
172	  const { bfcacheId } = useRouter()
173	  return <form key={bfcacheId}>{/* ... */}</form>
174	}
175	```
176	
177	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, the App Router preserves Client Component state across navigations using React `<Activity>`. Keying a component on `bfcacheId` resets it on each fresh navigation while still preserving its state across browser back/forward navigations. See [Preserving UI state](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for the recommended per-pattern resets.
178	
179	> **Good to know**:
180	> Instead of `bfcacheId`, prefer resetting state explicitly in an event handler (for example, `onSubmit`) or deriving a key from your data (for example, a draft id from the server). Use `bfcacheId` only as a last resort, like when migrating an existing codebase.
181	
182	## Version History
183	
184	| Version   | Changes                                                           |
185	| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
186	| `v15.4.0` | Optional `onInvalidate` callback for `router.prefetch` introduced |
187	| `v13.0.0` | `useRouter` from `next/navigation` introduced.                    |

89	  }, [pathname, searchParams])
90	
91	  return '...'
92	}
93	```
94	
95	Which can be imported into a layout.
96	
97	```jsx filename="app/layout.js" highlight={2,10-12}
98	import { Suspense } from 'react'
99	import { NavigationEvents } from './components/navigation-events'
100	
101	export default function Layout({ children }) {
102	  return (
103	    <html lang="en">
104	      <body>
105	        {children}
106	
107	        <Suspense fallback={null}>
108	          <NavigationEvents />
109	        </Suspense>
110	      </body>
111	    </html>
112	  )
113	}
114	```
115	
116	> **Good to know**: `<NavigationEvents>` is wrapped in a [`Suspense` boundary](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/loading#examples) because[`useSearchParams()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params) causes client-side rendering up to the closest `Suspense` boundary during [prerendering](/docs/app/glossary#prerendering). [Learn more](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/use-search-params#behavior).
117	
118	### Disabling scroll to top
119	
120	By default, Next.js will scroll to the top of the page when navigating to a new route. You can disable this behavior by passing `scroll: false` to `router.push()` or `router.replace()`.
121	
122	```tsx filename="app/example-client-component.tsx" switcher
123	'use client'
124	
125	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
126	
127	export default function Page() {
128	  const router = useRouter()
129	
130	  return (
131	    <button
132	      type="button"
133	      onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })}
134	    >
135	      Dashboard
136	    </button>
137	  )
138	}
139	```
140	
141	```jsx filename="app/example-client-component.jsx" switcher
142	'use client'
143	
144	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
145	
146	export default function Page() {
147	  const router = useRouter()
148	
149	  return (
150	    <button
151	      type="button"
152	      onClick={() => router.push('/dashboard', { scroll: false })}
153	    >
154	      Dashboard
155	    </button>
156	  )
157	}
158	```
159	
160	### `bfcacheId`
161	
162	`router.bfcacheId` is an opaque string identifier scoped to the current route segment. It changes when the surrounding segment is freshly created by a push or replace navigation, and stays the same for back/forward navigations, `router.refresh()`, and search-param- or hash-only navigations.
163	
164	The recommended use is to pass it as a React `key` to opt out of state preservation on fresh navigations, while still restoring it during a back/forward navigation:
165	
166	```tsx filename="app/example/page.tsx"
167	'use client'
168	
169	import { useRouter } from 'next/navigation'
170	
171	export default function Page() {
172	  const { bfcacheId } = useRouter()
173	  return <form key={bfcacheId}>{/* ... */}</form>
174	}
175	```
176	
177	When `cacheComponents` is enabled, the App Router preserves Client Component state across navigations using React `<Activity>`. Keying a component on `bfcacheId` resets it on each fresh navigation while still preserving its state across browser back/forward navigations. See [Preserving UI state](/docs/app/guides/preserving-ui-state) for the recommended per-pattern resets.
178	
179	> **Good to know**:
180	> Instead of `bfcacheId`, prefer resetting state explicitly in an event handler (for example, `onSubmit`) or deriving a key from your data (for example, a draft id from the server). Use `bfcacheId` only as a last resort, like when migrating an existing codebase.

events.content:
The migration is complete. Summary of what changed:

**Removed:** `pages/` directory entirely (all 9 files) and `styles/` (moved into `app/`).

**Added — App Router structure:**
- `app/layout.tsx` — root layout replacing `_app.js` + `_document.js`, using `next/font/google` (Inter) instead of manual `<link>` preconnect tags, and the `Metadata` API instead of `next/document`'s `<Head>`
- `app/page.tsx` — home page, `getServerSideProps` → async Server Component with `fetch(..., { cache: 'no-store' })`, `req.headers` → `headers()` from `next/headers`
- `app/blog/page.tsx` — `getStaticProps`/ISR → `fetch(..., { next: { revalidate: 60 } })`
- `app/blog/[id]/page.tsx` — `getStaticPaths`/`fallback: 'blocking'` → `generateStaticParams()` + default `dynamicParams`; `{ notFound: true }` → `notFound()`; `router.isFallback` removed (no longer needed); added `generateMetadata()` for per-post titles/OG tags
- `app/not-found.tsx` / `app/error.tsx` / `app/global-error.tsx` — replace `404.js`/`_error.js`'s `getInitialProps` pattern with the typed `error`/`retry` props (using the new stable `retry()` from v16.3+)
- `app/api/posts/route.ts`, `app/api/posts/[id]/route.ts` — `handler(req, res)` → named `GET`/`POST`/`PUT`/`DELETE` exports using Web `Request`/`Response.json()`; `context.params` is now `Promise<{id: string}>`; manual 405 fallback removed since App Router route handlers do this automatically

**Other:** `useRouter` migrated from `next/router` to `next/navigation` everywhere (dropped `isFallback`); raw `<a>` tags replaced with `next/link`'s `Link`; extracted small client-only islands (`NavigateButton`, `GoHomeButton`) since Server Component pages can't have `onClick` handlers directly; `components/AppProvider.js` converted to typed `.tsx` with `'use client'`; added `lib/types.ts` for shared `Post`/`Comment` types.

Verified with `tsc --noEmit` (clean), `next build` (all routes compiled with expected rendering strategies — dynamic home, ISR blog index, SSG blog details), and `next start` with live curl checks against every route including 404 cases and all API methods (200/201/400/404/405 all correct).
